Fill in the blank with an appropriate degree of comparison.
When comparing the two theories, Newton's laws were initially considered ___ acceptable. [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Use the comparative “less” when comparing two things.
Newton’s laws were considered less acceptable than the competing theory.
“Least” is superlative and requires more than two items.
“Lesser” generally modifies nouns, while “little” is the positive degree.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): less.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate degree of comparison.
Between the two musicians, I find Bach's compositions to be ___ profound. [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Use the comparative when comparing two items.
“More profound” compares Bach’s compositions with those of the other musician.
“Most” and “best” are superlatives and require a larger comparison set.
“Better” is grammatically comparative but does not modify “profound.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): more.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with appropriate parts of speech.
The soldiers, exhausted though they were, pressed on with an almost ___ fortitude. [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: An adjective modifies the noun “fortitude.”
“Mechanical” describes an automatic, unthinking display of endurance.
“Mechanically” is an adverb, “mechanize” is a verb, and “mechanic” is a noun.
Only “mechanical” fits the noun phrase.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): mechanical.

question.en:
Complete the sentence by choosing a suitable word to fill in the blank.
That she, of all people, ___ the one to criticize others is baffling. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The pronoun “she” takes the singular present verb “is.”
The parenthetical “of all people” does not affect agreement.
Completed sentence: “That she, of all people, is the one to criticize others is baffling.”
“Are” and “were” do not fit; “be” is not the finite indicative form.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): is.

question.en:
Improve the sentence by selecting the appropriate preposition from the following options.
We need to plan carefully to stay ___ of our competition. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Ahead of” means in front of or performing better than competitors.
Correct sentence: “We need to plan carefully to stay ahead of our competition.”
“For,” “in” and “beyond” do not form this standard phrase.
Careful planning helps maintain a competitive lead.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): ahead.

question.en:
Select the correct option:
The grant allowed researchers to delve ___ topics previously considered fringe. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Delve into” means investigate or examine deeply.
Correct sentence: “The grant allowed researchers to delve into topics previously considered fringe.”
“Onto,” “in” and “about” do not form the standard phrasal verb.
The researchers investigate neglected subjects in depth.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): into.

question.en:
Complete the collocation by choosing a suitable word to fill in the blank.
The lawyer managed to ___ access to confidential documents. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Collocation: “Gain access to” means succeed in obtaining entry or permission.
The lawyer gained access to confidential documents.
“Obtain” and “receive” do not idiomatically precede “access to” in this structure.
“Attain” usually takes goals, levels or positions.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): gain.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with appropriate parts of speech.
The scientist was awarded a medal ___ her groundbreaking contributions to molecular biology. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Owing to” is a preposition meaning because of and is followed by a noun phrase.
The award was given because of her contributions.
“Because,” “although” and “lest” require clauses rather than the noun phrase “her groundbreaking contributions.”
Only “owing to” fits grammatically.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): owing to.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate tense.
If technological advancements ___ at the current pace, we will soon witness innovations previously deemed impossible. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: A real future condition uses simple present in the if-clause and “will” in the result.
The plural subject “advancements” takes “continue.”
“Continued” and “had continued” introduce unreal or past conditions.
“Have continued” is unnecessary for the standard first conditional.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): continue.

question.en:
Fill in the blanks with the correct option, ensuring the verb tenses accurately reflect the chronological sequence of events.
Scarcely ___ the morning train when I realized that, if I had left my house five minutes later, I ___ the crucial interview. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 3]

2.en: had I boarded, would have missed

solution.en:
Rule: “Scarcely” triggers inversion; an unreal past condition uses “would have + past participle.”
“Had I boarded” gives the required inversion after “scarcely.”
The missed interview is the unreal past result, so “would have missed” is correct.
The other options lack the required inversion or conditional form.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): had I boarded, would have missed.

question.en:
Choose the option that provides the correct sequence of prepositions to complete the sentence grammatically.
The philosopher contended that morality exists ___ the realm of legality, operates ___ opposition to utilitarianism, and persists ___ spite of cultural relativism. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Correct phrases: “beyond the realm of,” “in opposition to,” and “in spite of.”
“Beyond” places morality outside legality; “in opposition to” expresses conflict with utilitarianism.
“In spite of” means despite cultural relativism.
The other sequences do not produce these standard expressions.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): beyond, in, in.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
Tomorrow, I ___ the dusty old book from the attic and relive my favorite childhood memories. [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Tomorrow” requires a future form for the intended action.
“Will open” expresses the planned future action and parallels “relive.”
“Would open” is conditional, “am open” describes a state, and “opened” is past.
Only “will open” fits the time reference.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): will open.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
I managed to find my way to the museum only ___ a tattered paper map and a few landmarks. [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
By means of (के माध्यम से) = using something as a method.
The traveller used a tattered map and landmarks to find the museum.
“Beneath” indicates position, “following the path” does not fit the map phrase, and “barring” means except.
Only “by means of” expresses the method.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): by means of.

tests.title: CGL 2026 Fill in the Blanks PART-3

listing.title: CGL 2026 Fill in the Blanks PART-3

meta.title: SSC 2026 ENGLISH FILL IN THE BLANKS

question.en:
Complete the collocation by choosing a suitable word to fill in the blank.
Many professionals find it difficult to ___ a balance between work and personal life. [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Collocation: “Strike a balance between” means achieve a satisfactory compromise.
Professionals try to balance work and personal life.
“Keep a balance” is possible but less precise than the established collocation “strike a balance.”
“Set” and “form” are not idiomatic here.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): strike.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate tense.
Were the data ___ earlier, corrective measures could have been implemented. [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Were + subject + past participle” forms an inverted unreal-past passive condition.
The data did not perform the analysis, so the passive “analyzed thoroughly” is required.
“Had analyzed” would be active and lacks an agent; “were analyzed” duplicates “were.”
The base form “analyze” cannot complete the passive construction.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): analyzed thoroughly.

question.en:
Fill in the blanks with the appropriate article.
Although ___ emergence of artificial intelligence promises significant benefits, it also raises ___ host of ethical dilemmas. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “The” is used for a specific thing; “a host of” is a fixed expression meaning “a large number of”.
“The emergence of artificial intelligence” refers to one particular development, so it takes “the”.
“A host of ethical dilemmas” is the fixed phrase; “the host of” changes the meaning to a specific host.
Correct sentence: Although the emergence of artificial intelligence promises significant benefits, it also raises a host of ethical dilemmas.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): the, a.

Note: SSC's official answer key marked option (4): the, the as correct, which is logically incorrect. This is a bonus question.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
I ___ the defective laptop to the store before I realized I had left my charger at home. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Past perfect marks the action completed before the later realization.
The laptop was returned before the speaker realized the charger was missing.
“I had returned” correctly orders the two past events.
Simple past, past continuous and present perfect do not establish the sequence as precisely.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): had returned.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
I ___ the local market this weekend to restock the pantry before the busy work week begins. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Will + base verb” expresses a future plan.
“This weekend” and the future purpose of restocking require “will visit.”
“Would visit” is conditional, “visiting” is non-finite, and “visited” is past.
The future simple is appropriate.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): will visit.

question.en:
In the following sentence, four alternatives are given for the two blanks. Choose the most appropriate alternative to complete the sentence meaningfully and grammatically.
The theoretical model proposed by the committee underscores the necessity ___ methodological flexibility while simultaneously ___ epistemic biases that often distort empirical interpretation. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Necessity of + gerund” and “while + present participle” are appropriate.
“Of adopting” follows the noun “necessity.”
“Mitigating” is parallel to the implied subject and the adverb “simultaneously.”
The infinitive and perfect alternatives do not fit both structures.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): of adopting, mitigating.

question.en:
In the following question, a sentence with three blanks is given. Choose the most appropriate option that fills all the blanks correctly and meaningfully.
The director's ___ reinterpretation of the classic tale, coupled with a ___ cinematographic palette and ___ pacing, divided both critics and audiences. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Audacious (साहसी) = bold and inventive.
A bold reinterpretation with a muted visual palette and deliberate pacing can divide opinion.
The adjectives in B form a coherent artistic description.
The other sets introduce contradictory or less meaningful combinations.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): audacious, muted, deliberate.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
His recent paper is as ___ as any ever published in the journal's history. [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “As + positive adjective + as” expresses equality.
“As insightful as” compares the paper with any other in the journal’s history.
Comparative and superlative forms do not fit this construction.
“Insightfully” is an adverb, but an adjective is required.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): insightful.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The speaker's tone, marked by sarcastic inflections, stood in stark ___ to the solemnity of the occasion. [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Collocation: “Stand in stark contrast to” = be strikingly different from.
Sarcasm contrasted sharply with the solemn occasion.
“Proportion” concerns relative size, and “parallel” implies similarity.
“Deference” means respectful submission.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): contrast.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The speaker's rhetoric was replete with appeals to emotion but lacked the ___ of empirical substantiation. [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rigor (यथार्थता/कठोर परिश्रम) = strict precision and thoroughness.
Emotional rhetoric lacked the rigor of empirical support.
“Depth” is possible generally but does not express methodological exactness.
Tone and validity do not fit the possessive construction as precisely.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): rigor.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
His consistent refusal to acknowledge empirical evidence reflects a dangerous ___ to ideological rigidity. [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Adherence (अनुपालन) = firm attachment to a belief or practice.
“Adherence to ideological rigidity” fits the refusal to consider evidence.
“Resistance to” would mean opposition, reversing the meaning.
Deference and contribution do not fit the context.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): adherence.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The consultant’s prognosis, though optimistic, failed to ___ the structural weaknesses evident in the model. [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Address (संबोधित करना) = deal with a problem.
The optimistic prognosis failed to address evident structural weaknesses.
“Diagnose” means identify, “predict” means forecast, and “relieve” means alleviate.
Only “address” conveys engaging with the weaknesses.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): address.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
No strategy was found to be ___ than diversification during the crisis. [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Than” requires the comparative adjective “more effective.”
Diversification was more effective than every other strategy during the crisis.
The positive and superlative forms do not fit “than.”
“Effectively” is an adverb, but an adjective is required.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): more effective.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The treaty was hailed as a breakthrough despite its ___ language that allowed for multiple interpretations. [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Ambiguous (अनेकार्थी) = open to multiple interpretations.
The treaty’s ambiguous language allowed different readings.
“Concise” means brief, “forthright” means direct, and “implicit” means implied.
Only “ambiguous” directly matches the explanation.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): ambiguous.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The committee's reluctance to engage directly with dissenting voices was seen as a tacit ___ of accountability. [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Evasion (टालना) = avoidance.
Avoiding dissenting voices amounts to a tacit evasion of accountability.
Invocation (आह्वान) = appeal
Revision (संशोधन) = amendment; expansion (विस्तार) = enlargement

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): evasion.

question.en:
Fill in the blanks with an appropriate degree of comparison.
Seldom have we encountered a theory ___ intriguing ___ this one. [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Comparative adjective + “than” compares two theories.
“More intriguing than this one” is the correct construction.
“Much … than” and “more … as” are ungrammatical.
“As … that” does not form the required comparison.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): more, than.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate tense.
If the team ___ the interim results more meticulously, the final report would not have contained so many discrepancies. [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Third conditional uses “if + past perfect” and “would have + past participle.”
“Had analyzed” expresses the unreal past condition.
The result “would not have contained” confirms the counterfactual structure.
The other forms do not fit.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): had analyzed.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate tense.
Although the panel ___ several contentious issues during the discussion, it failed to reach a unanimous conclusion. [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Simple past describes the completed discussion.
“Addressed” parallels “failed” in the main clause.
Simple present and past perfect create unsuitable time relations.
Past continuous would emphasize an unfinished background action.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): addressed.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correct collocation:
The NGO took ___ the responsibility of educating underprivileged children in rural areas. [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Take on (जिम्मेदारी लेना) = accept a duty or responsibility.
The NGO took on responsibility for educating rural children.
“Take in” means absorb or deceive, “take off” means depart.
“Take out” means remove.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): on.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
Her remarks were not only misinformed but also ___, undermining years of community-led advocacy. [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Derogatory (अपमानजनक) = insulting or disparaging.
Derogatory remarks could undermine community advocacy.
“Contentious” means controversial, which need not be damaging.
Illustrative and preliminary do not fit the negative parallel.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): derogatory.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
The Prime Minister emphasised the importance of digital literacy ___ rural women to bridge the digital divide. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Among (के बीच) = within a group.
Digital literacy is to be promoted among rural women.
“After” indicates time, “with” accompaniment, and “across” a span or movement.
Only “among” identifies the target population.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): among.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition.
The agreement remained ___ abeyance until further notice. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Collocation: “In abeyance” means temporarily suspended.
The agreement remained inactive until further notice.
“At,” “on” and “under” do not form the standard phrase.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): in.

question.en:
Complete the sentence by choosing a suitable word to fill in the blank.
Neither the manager nor his assistants ___ prepared for the sudden audit. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: With “neither … nor,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
The nearer subject “assistants” is plural.
“Were prepared” also fits the past context of the sudden audit.
The other options do not provide plural past agreement.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): were.

question.en:
Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate combination of articles and verb form.
It is imperative that ___ anonymity of the whistle-blower ___ maintained, as even ___ slightest leak could compromise the entire federal investigation. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Mandative “imperative” takes the base subjunctive “be.”
Specific anonymity takes “the,” and “the slightest” is a fixed emphatic phrase.
“The anonymity … be maintained” is correct.
The other combinations use the wrong article or indicative verb.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): the, be, the.

question.en:
Choose the correct option to complete the sentence meaningfully and grammatically.
The director ___ the entire script multiple times before the producers finally ___ it last week. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Past perfect marks repeated rewriting before the later approval.
The producers approved the script last week in simple past.
The director had rewritten it multiple times before that point.
Only B establishes the sequence correctly.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): had rewritten, approved.

tests.title: CGL 2026 Fill in the Blanks PART-4

listing.title: CGL 2026 Fill in the Blanks PART-4

meta.title: SSC 2026 ENGLISH FILL IN THE BLANKS

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition.
The event transpired ___ circumstances still unknown to the public. [SSC CGL 27/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Collocation: “under … circumstances” = in particular conditions.
The fixed phrase is “under circumstances”: The event transpired under circumstances still unknown to the public.
“Amidst” means surrounded by (used with events or crowds, not “circumstances” in this sense); “within” and “inside” show containment.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): under.

Note: SSC's official answer key marked option (2): amidst as correct, which is logically incorrect. This is a bonus question.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with appropriate parts of speech.
The committee's decision was met with widespread ___ among the academic community, although some dissenters voiced their reservations. [SSC CGL 27/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Acclaim (प्रशंसा) = public praise.
The adjective “widespread” and preposition “with” require the noun “acclaim.”
“Acclaimed” is a verb or adjective, and “acclaiming” a participle.
“Acclimated” means adapted.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): acclaim.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The report's language, laden with technical jargon, served more to ___ than to inform the general public. [SSC CGL 27/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Obfuscate (अस्पष्ट करना) = make unclear.
Jargon obscured rather than informed the general public.
Illuminate and clarify mean make clear.
Communicate is too general and lacks the intended contrast.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): obfuscate.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
Although framed as reformist, the policy inadvertently ___ structural inequalities rather than mitigating them. [SSC CGL 27/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Perpetuate (बनाए रखना) = cause something to continue.
The policy unintentionally perpetuated inequalities instead of reducing them.
“Repelled” means drove away, and “suppressed” means restrained.
“Amplified” means intensified but is not the keyed choice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): perpetuated.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The ambassador's statement was meticulously phrased to maintain diplomatic decorum while subtly ___ criticism. [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Inject (डालना) = introduce an element subtly.
The ambassador inserted criticism without violating diplomatic decorum.
“Deflecting” means turning criticism away.
“Inflicting” means imposing harm, and “reflecting” means showing.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): injecting.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate adverb.
The scholar spoke ___, preferring depth to flamboyance. [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Thus (इस प्रकार) = in this manner.
The scholar spoke in the manner described: with depth rather than flamboyance.
“Within” refers to location, “onward” to forward movement.
“Amiss” means wrongly.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): thus.

question.en:
Fill in the blanks in the following sentence with the most appropriate set of words to form a grammatically correct and meaningful sentence.
___ the central bank intervened more decisively during the liquidity crisis, the cascading defaults that ___ the financial sector would have been largely contained, and investor confidence ___ so dramatically. [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 3]

1.en: Had, crippled, would not have eroded

2.en: Should, crippled, would not have eroded

3.en: If, had crippled, would not erode

4.en: Had, crippling, would not have eroded

solution.en:
Rule: Inverted third conditional = “Had + subject + past participle.”
“Had the central bank intervened …” expresses an unreal past condition.
“Crippled” describes the defaults, and “would not have eroded” gives the unreal result.
Only A supplies all three correct forms.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): Had, crippled, would not have eroded.

question.en:
Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate option to make the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful.
It was ___ undeniable irony that ___ man once celebrated as ___ architect of peace should become the very symbol of conflict. [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Undeniable” begins with a vowel sound, so use “an.”
“The man” is identified by the following descriptive clause.
“An architect of peace” introduces his former role nonspecifically.
The required sequence is “an, the, an.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): an, the, an.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
It is high time the minister (1)/ clarifies his stance on the matter (2)/ rather than leaving it (3)/ open to public speculation. (4) [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: 'It is high time' + subject is followed by the simple past (subjunctive) form of the verb.
'clarifies' in part (2) must be 'clarified'.
Correct sentence: It is high time the minister clarified his stance on the matter rather than leaving it open to public speculation.
Parts (1), (3) and (4) are correct: 'rather than + leaving' and 'open to public speculation' are idiomatic.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Read the sentences below carefully and identify which one contains a grammatical or structural error.

(P) Professor Ali’s latest historical monograph is more comprehensive than concise, offering exhaustive archival data at the expense of brevity.

(Q) The lead prosecutor remarked that the defendant's sudden courtroom confession was ready than calculated, catching the entire defence team off guard. [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: When two qualities of the same thing are compared, use 'more + adjective + than + adjective'.
(P) 'more comprehensive than concise' follows the rule – correct.
(Q) 'was ready than calculated' has 'than' without a comparative. It should be 'was more ready than calculated'.
So only Q contains an error.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): Only Q.

question.en:
Read the following sentences carefully and identify which one contains a grammatical or structural error.

(P) The department seeks an administrative director more capable of managing international logistics than of drafting internal fiscal policies.

(Q) A legal framework less adaptive to technological disruption than intent on preserving historical precedents will inevitably stifle industrial innovation. [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: In a comparison of two qualities, both sides must be parallel in form.
(P) 'more capable of managing … than of drafting' – both sides take 'of + -ing'; correct.
(Q) 'less adaptive to … than intent on …' – two adjectives with their prepositions, and the subject 'A legal framework' agrees with 'will … stifle'; correct.
Neither sentence has an error.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): Neither P nor Q.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.

The committee decided their decision. [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: 'decision' collocates with 'make', 'take' or 'announce', not 'decide' (decide a decision is redundant).
The error is the verb 'decided'.
Correct sentence: The committee made / announced their decision.
'committee' – correct subject
'their' – a collective noun acting as individuals may take 'their'
'decision' – correct object

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): decided.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.

You should write clear so that the reader understands. [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The verb 'write' must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. 'Clear' is an adjective, so it should be replaced by the adverb 'clearly'.

Correct sentence: You should write clearly so that the reader understands.

Note: This question was logically wrong as given by SSC (the official answer key does not match the actual error) and was treated as a bonus question.
solution.hi:
क्रिया 'write' को विशेषण (adjective) नहीं, बल्कि क्रिया-विशेषण (adverb) modify करता है। 'Clear' एक adjective है, इसलिए इसे adverb 'clearly' से बदला जाना चाहिए।

सही वाक्य: You should write clearly so that the reader understands.

नोट: SSC द्वारा दिया गया यह प्रश्न तार्किक रूप से गलत था (आधिकारिक उत्तर वास्तविक त्रुटि से मेल नहीं खाता) और इसे बोनस प्रश्न माना गया।

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
All the equipments (1)/ needed for the installation (2)/ were procured (3)/ well in advance. (4) [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: 'Equipment' is an uncountable noun – it has no plural form and takes a singular verb.
Part (1) 'equipments' should be 'equipment'; the verb in part (3) then becomes 'was'.
Correct sentence: All the equipment needed for the installation was procured well in advance.
Parts (2) and (4) are correct; part (3) changes only as a result of the error in part (1).

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Although the results appear encouraging on the surface, (1)/ yet critics remain sceptical of the methods (2)/ employed in gathering and interpreting (3)/ the underlying datasets. (4) [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: 'Although/Though' is not followed by 'yet' or 'but' in the main clause; one conjunction is enough.
Part (2) begins with 'yet', which must be removed.
Correct sentence: Although the results appear encouraging on the surface, critics remain sceptical of the methods employed in gathering and interpreting the underlying datasets.
Parts (1), (3) and (4) are correct; 'sceptical of' is the right preposition.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.

He was late to an meeting scheduled at 9 AM. [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: 'a' is used before a consonant sound and 'an' before a vowel sound.
'meeting' begins with the consonant sound /m/, so the article must be 'a'.
Correct sentence: He was late to a meeting scheduled at 9 AM.
'late', 'meeting' and 'scheduled' are used correctly.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): an.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.

He is more smarter than anyone else in class. [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: A double comparative is wrong – use either '-er' or 'more', never both.
'smarter' is already comparative, so 'more' must be removed.
Correct sentence: He is smarter than anyone else in class.
'anyone else' is correct in a comparison within the same group; 'class' is correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): more.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.

We reached to a conclusion after the meeting. [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: 'reach' is a transitive verb and takes a direct object without 'to'.
'reached to a conclusion' is wrong; the preposition 'to' must be removed.
Correct sentence: We reached a conclusion after the meeting.
'reached', 'conclusion' and 'meeting' are used correctly.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): to.

question.en:
Choose the error in the sentence.

The medicine had a strong affect on her recovery. [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: 'Effect' (प्रभाव) is the noun; 'affect' (प्रभावित करना) is usually the verb.
After the article 'a strong', a noun is needed, so 'affect' must be 'effect'.
Correct sentence: The medicine had a strong effect on her recovery.
'medicine', 'strong' and 'recovery' are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): affect.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The professor recommended that each of the selected candidates (1)/ submit their thesis proposal by next Friday (2)/ failing which the slot would be offered to waitlisted scholars. (3)/ No error (4) [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: 'Each of + plural noun' is singular and takes a singular pronoun (his or her), not 'their'.
'submit' is correct (subjunctive after 'recommended that'), but 'their' in part (2) does not agree with 'each'.
Correct sentence: The professor recommended that each of the selected candidates submit his or her thesis proposal by next Friday…
Part (1) – 'each of the selected candidates' is correct
Part (3) – 'failing which' and 'would be offered' are correct

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Spot the error in the following sentence and identify the INCORRECT part.

He has been afraid from spiders since childhood. [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective 'afraid' takes the preposition 'of'.
'afraid from' is wrong.
Correct sentence: He has been afraid of spiders since childhood.
'spiders' – correct plural noun
'since childhood' – 'since' correctly marks a point of time with the present perfect

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): afraid from.

question.en:
Spot the error in the following sentence and identify the INCORRECT part.

She always avoids to speak during the meetings because she is shy. [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: 'avoid' is followed by a gerund (V-ing), not a to-infinitive.
'avoids to speak' must be 'avoids speaking'.
Correct sentence: She always avoids speaking during the meetings because she is shy.
'always avoids' – correct verb with singular subject
'during the meetings' – correct preposition

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): to speak.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.

She’s reading an Times of India editorial. [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: 'an' is used before a vowel sound; 'Times' begins with the consonant sound /t/.
The article must be 'a' (or 'the' before the name of the newspaper).
Correct sentence: She's reading a Times of India editorial.
'reading', 'India' and 'editorial' are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): an.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
She wore a stunning red silk long scarf (1) that complemented her traditional attire (2) during the award ceremony (3) at the convention centre. (4) [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Order of adjectives – opinion, size/length, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose + noun.
In part (1) 'long' (size) must come before 'red' (colour) and 'silk' (material).
Correct sentence: She wore a stunning long red silk scarf that complemented her traditional attire during the award ceremony at the convention centre.
Parts (2), (3) and (4) are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
It seems as though the department is reluctant (1)/ not because of the cost implications, (2)/ but because that it might signal (3)/ a policy shift they are not ready to make. (4) [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: 'because' is itself a conjunction; it is not followed by 'that'.
Part (3) 'because that it might' must be 'because it might'.
Correct sentence: …not because of the cost implications, but because it might signal a policy shift they are not ready to make.
Part (1) 'as though' is correct; part (2) 'because of + noun' is correct; part (4) is correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): (3).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.

He paid a heavy apology after the incident. [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: 'apology' collocates with adjectives like 'sincere', 'deep' or 'profuse', not 'heavy'.
'heavy' goes with words like 'price', 'loss' or 'fine' (a heavy price), so it is the wrong adjective here.
Correct sentence: He paid a sincere apology after the incident.
'paid' – 'pay one's apologies' is an accepted formal expression
'apology' and 'incident' are correct nouns

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): heavy.

question.en:
Read the sentences provided in options A, B, C, and D carefully. While three of the sentences are grammatically sound, one contains an “article usage” error. Identify the option with the error.
A. A research team at the University of Cambridge successfully engineered a stable topological qubit, outpacing rival physics departments across Europe.
B. Excavations funded by Yale University unearthed a beautifully preserved fossilised apex predator in the badlands of Montana.
C. While the Administrator refused to comment on the launch failure, Director General Faiz issued a comprehensive technical briefing to the press.
D. The diplomatic delegation travelled from Netherlands to the Czech Republic to ratify the new maritime trade agreement. [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 3]

1.en: A research team at the University of Cambridge successfully engineered a stable topological qubit, outpacing rival physics departments across Europe.

2.en: Excavations funded by Yale University unearthed a beautifully preserved fossilised apex predator in the badlands of Montana.

3.en: While the Administrator refused to comment on the launch failure, Director General Faiz issued a comprehensive technical briefing to the press.

4.en: The diplomatic delegation travelled from Netherlands to the Czech Republic to ratify the new maritime trade agreement.

solution.en:
Rule: The definite article “the” is used with “Netherlands.”
Option D should read “travelled from the Netherlands to the Czech Republic.”
“The University of Cambridge” is correctly used in A.
No article is required before “Yale University” or “Montana” in B; C uses its articles and titles appropriately.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): The diplomatic delegation travelled from Netherlands to the Czech Republic to ratify the new maritime trade agreement.

question.en:
Read the sentences below carefully and identify which one contains a grammatical or structural error.
(P) The agricultural collective harvested as many more metric tons of organic grain than the commercial farming conglomerate during the fiscal year.
(Q) The more thoroughly the research cohort analysed the genomic sequencing data, the fewer anomalies they found in the control group. [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Equality uses “as + adjective + as,” not “as … than.”
P mixes two comparative structures. Use either “as many metric tons … as” or “more metric tons … than.”
Q correctly uses the paired comparative structure “The more thoroughly …, the fewer ….”
Therefore, only P is erroneous.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): Only P.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
He speaks too much fast for me to understand. [SSC CGL 07/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Too” directly modifies the adverb “fast”; “much” is redundant.
The erroneous part is “much.”
Correct sentence: “He speaks too fast for me to understand.”
“Speaks,” “fast” and “understand” are all grammatically appropriate in the corrected structure.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): much.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
A Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world. [SSC CGL 07/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: No indefinite article is used before the proper name of a mountain.
“Mount Everest” is a proper noun, so the initial “A” is incorrect.
Correct sentence: “Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world.”
“Everest,” the superlative “highest” and “world” are correctly used.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): A.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
A earth revolves around the sun. [SSC CGL 07/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Use the definite article “the” with unique celestial bodies such as the earth and the sun.
The erroneous part is “A,” which must be replaced by “The.”
Correct sentence: “The earth revolves around the sun.”
The singular verb “revolves” correctly agrees with “earth.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): A.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
This is the most easiest question in the test. [SSC CGL 07/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Do not use “most” before a superlative already ending in “-est.”
“Easiest” is already the superlative of “easy,” so “most” is erroneous.
Correct sentence: “This is the easiest question in the test.”
“Question” and “test” are grammatically correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): most.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
We were leave for the airport when the storm began. [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing.
After “were,” the verb must be “leaving,” not the base form “leave.”
Correct sentence: “We were leaving for the airport when the storm began.”
“Storm,” “began” and “airport” are correctly used.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): leave.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The editor-in-chief asked whether (1)/ the article had underwent (2)/ plagiarism screening (3)/ before approval. (4) [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: After “had,” use the past participle “undergone.”
“Underwent” is the simple past, so part (2) is erroneous.
Correct phrase: “the article had undergone plagiarism screening.”
The other parts contain no grammatical error.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The tribunal objected to not the content of the testimony (1)/ but the manner in which it was introduced (2)/ without any authentication by the official registrar (3)/ or acknowledgment of its provenance. (4) [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: In the correlative structure “not … but,” “not” must precede the object directly.
Part (1) should read “The tribunal objected not to the content of the testimony.”
The contrast is then correctly completed by “but the manner ….”
Parts (2), (3) and (4) are structurally sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
The team have completed their project ahead of schedule [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: A collective noun treated as one unit takes a singular verb.
Here “the team” acts as a single body, so “has” is required.
Correct sentence: “The team has completed their project ahead of schedule.”
The remaining words are grammatically sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): have.

question.en:
Spot the error in the following sentence and identify the INCORRECT part.
She prefers coffee than tea in the morning. [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Prefer” takes “to,” not “than,” when comparing two nouns.
The error lies in “than tea.”
Correct sentence: “She prefers coffee to tea in the morning.”
The other parts are grammatically correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): than tea.

question.en:
Spot the error in the following sentence and identify the INCORRECT part.
She insisted me to attend the meeting at any cost. [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Insist” takes “on + gerund” or a that-clause, not an object followed by an infinitive.
The erroneous part is “insisted me to.”
Correct sentence: “She insisted on my attending the meeting at any cost.”
One may also write “insisted that I attend.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): insisted me to.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Each applicant must bring his or her ID proof (1)/ and fill the necessary documents (2)/ prior to the final evaluation round (3)/ scheduled this Friday. (4)/ [SSC CGL 09/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The standard collocation is “fill in/out a form,” not “fill documents.”
Part (2) should read “fill in the necessary forms” or “complete the necessary documents.”
The error lies in the verb–object combination.
The remaining parts are grammatically acceptable.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
There are less than twenty applicants (1)/ who meet the eligibility criteria (2)/ for the advanced fellowship (3)/ offered by the institute. (4)/ [SSC CGL 09/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Use “fewer” with countable plural nouns.
“Applicants” is countable, so part (1) must read “There are fewer than twenty applicants.”
“Less” is used with uncountable quantities.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
She didn't went to the seminar last week. [SSC CGL 09/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: After “didn’t,” use the base form of the verb.
“Went” is the simple past and must be replaced by “go.”
Correct sentence: “She didn’t go to the seminar last week.”
The other parts contain no error.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): went.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The correlation-matrix visualization (1)/ appeared more clear (2)/ when the superfluous variables were removed (3)/ during the second iteration of analysis. (4)/ [SSC CGL 09/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: The comparative of “clear” is “clearer.”
Part (2) should read “appeared clearer,” not “more clear.”
The comparison concerns the visualization before and after variables were removed.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
She completed the assignment quick to meet the deadline. [SSC CGL 09/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Use an adverb to modify the verb “completed.”
“Quick” is an adjective, so the erroneous word is “quick.”
Correct sentence: “She completed the assignment quickly to meet the deadline.”
The other words are grammatically correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): quick.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence
He passed away the forms to the candidates. [SSC CGL 09/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Pass out” means distribute; “pass away” means die.
The erroneous word is “away.”
Correct sentence: “He passed out the forms to the candidates.”
“Forms” and “candidates” are appropriate objects in this context.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): away.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
He was complete ignored by the team during the discussion. [SSC CGL 10/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Use an adverb to modify the passive verb “was ignored.”
“Complete” is an adjective and must become “completely.”
Correct sentence: “He was completely ignored by the team during the discussion.”
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): complete.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
She has the rare ability (1)/ of making complex theories (2)/ sound simple (3)/ and intuitively clear. (4) [SSC CGL 10/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Ability” is followed by the infinitive “to + base verb.”
Part (2) should read “to make complex theories,” not “of making.”
“Make + object + adjective” correctly produces “make complex theories sound simple.”
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
What the consultant suggested implementing (1)/ was a method that would reduce redundancies (2)/ and optimize interdepartmental workflows (3)/ without requiring additional fundings. (4) [SSC CGL 10/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Funding” is uncountable in the sense of financial resources.
Part (4) should read “additional funding,” not “fundings.”
The method would reduce redundancy and optimize workflows without extra financial support.
The other parts are grammatically sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): (4).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The vice-chancellor insisted that the policy (1)/ is to be revised (2)/ by the end of the quarter (3)/ to address the audit remarks. (4) [SSC CGL 10/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: After “insisted that,” use the mandative subjunctive “be + past participle.”
Part (2) should read “the policy be revised,” not “is to be revised.”
“Should be revised” would also be correct.
The other parts are grammatically sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
A very few researchers (1)/ have attempted to replicate the study (2)/ under identical field conditions (3)/ due to logistical limitations. (4) [SSC CGL 10/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Very few” means a small number; the article “a” changes the intended expression.
Part (1) should read “Very few researchers.”
“A few” means some, while “very few” emphasizes scarcity.
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a lexical error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: The sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) Maintaining a posture of strict non-disclosure, the board of directors refuses to comment on the acquisition / (Q) even though rumours bound that the tech giant is on the verge of bankruptcy / (R) due to severe algorithmic failures that have fundamentally compromised / (S) its core proprietary architecture. [SSC CGL 10/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Lexical error: “Bound” should be “abound.”
“Abound” means exist in large numbers, which fits “rumours abound.”
Therefore, segment Q contains the error.
The remaining segments use their vocabulary correctly.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): Q.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a lexical error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: The sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) The coalition launched an aggressive media campaign to garter support / (Q) for the proposed labour reforms, seeking to mobilise constituent pressure /(R) and thereby influence critical swing-vote lawmakers whose final deliberations / (S) will dictate the outcome of the fast-approaching, high-stakes parliamentary vote. [SSC CGL 10/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Lexical error: “Garter” should be “garner.”
“Garner support” means gather or obtain support.
“Garter” is an item of clothing, so segment P is erroneous.
The remaining segments are lexically sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): P.

question.en:
Choose the error in the sentence.
The teacher emphasized on the importance of time management. [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Emphasize” is a transitive verb and takes a direct object without “on.”
The erroneous word is “on.”
Correct sentence: “The teacher emphasized the importance of time management.”
The remaining words are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): on.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Each of the candidates (1)/ are expected to carry (2)/ their original ID proofs (3)/ for verification. (4)/ [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Each” is singular and takes a singular verb.
Part (2) should read “is expected to carry,” not “are expected.”
The plural “candidates” does not control agreement after “each of.”
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
Her performance was extremely excellence throughout the quarter. [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: The adverb “extremely” must modify an adjective, not a noun.
“Excellence” is a noun and should become “excellent.”
Correct sentence: “Her performance was extremely excellent throughout the quarter.”
The other words are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): excellence.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
I have a strongly feeling that something's off. [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: An adjective modifies the noun “feeling.”
“Strongly” is an adverb and must become “strong.”
Correct sentence: “I have a strong feeling that something’s off.”
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): strongly.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
What critics often overlook (1)/ is not the literary structure per se, (2)/ but the emotional authenticity of characters (3)/ and how it affects reader's trust. (4) [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Use the plural possessive when referring to readers generally.
Part (4) should read “readers’ trust,” with the apostrophe after the plural “s.”
The singular “reader’s trust” does not fit the general reference.
The remaining parts are grammatically sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): (4).

question.en:
Identify the word in this sentence that contains an error.
He was accused for cheating in the final exam. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Accuse somebody of something” is the fixed construction.
The erroneous word is “for,” which must become “of.”
Correct sentence: “He was accused of cheating in the final exam.”
The remaining words are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): for.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The judge not only dismissed the petition (1)/ but also reprimanding the lawyer (2)/ for misrepresenting facts (3)/ during the cross-examination. (4) [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Not only … but also” must join parallel verb forms.
“Dismissed” is a finite past-tense verb, so part (2) should read “but also reprimanded the lawyer.”
“Reprimanding” breaks the parallelism.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
While the director had hoped for clarity, (1)/ what emerged instead were overlapping interpretations (2)/ that undermined the coherence (3)/ of the original draft. (4) [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The subject “what emerged” is a singular nominal clause.
Part (2) should read “what emerged instead was overlapping interpretations.”
The complement may be plural, but the verb agrees with the singular what-clause.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
No less than five hundred students (1)/ has enrolled in (2)/ the online preparatory course (3)/ for civil service exams. (4) [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: The plural subject “five hundred students” takes a plural verb.
Part (2) should read “have enrolled in.”
“No less than” emphasizes the number but does not make the subject singular.
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Rarely the department issues (1)/ such open calls for proposals (2)/ without internal approvals (3)/ from the steering committee. (4) [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Negative adverbials such as “rarely” require subject–auxiliary inversion at the start of a clause.
Part (1) should read “Rarely does the department issue ….”
The given order incorrectly retains ordinary statement order.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
The sentence below is divided into two parts labelled P and Q. Identify which sentence contains a grammatical or idiomatic error.
P: The corporate legal team meticulously ironed out the final merger documents with the target firm's underwriters before the executive board signed them.
Q: During the high-pressure restructuring session in the unventilated boardroom, the junior analyst suddenly passed out from heat exhaustion. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Both sentences use their phrasal verbs correctly.
“Ironed out” means resolved difficulties or finalized details.
“Passed out” means lost consciousness, which fits heat exhaustion.
Neither P nor Q contains a grammatical or idiomatic error.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): Neither P nor Q.

question.en:
Read the two sentences given below carefully and identify which one contains a grammatical error.
P: The target software corporation implemented an aggressive poison-pill strategy to fend off against the hostile takeover bid initiated by the activist hedge fund.
Q: During the cross-border corporate fraud investigation, the forensic accounting team began to home in on the anomalous shell company transactions routed through offshore tax havens. [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Fend off” is transitive and does not take “against.”
P should read “to fend off the hostile takeover bid.”
Q correctly uses “home in on,” meaning focus attention on a target.
Therefore, only P contains an error.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): Only P.

question.en: Read the sentences provided in options A, B, C, and D carefully. While three of the sentences are grammatically sound, one contains an “article usage” error. Identify the option with the error. [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A trireme was a highly manoeuvrable ancient warship powered by the three rows of oars, designed by Mediterranean civilisations.

2.en: Following the catastrophic volcanic eruption on the island, the displaced were immediately provided with temporary shelter.

3.en: Mangroves protect vulnerable coastlines from severe tidal erosion by trapping sediment within their complex, intertwined root structures.

4.en: The blue whale is considered the largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth, occupying an apex position within marine ecosystems.

solution.en:
Rule: Do not use “the” before a simple numerical description unless the items are specifically identified.
Option A should read “powered by three rows of oars,” not “the three rows.”
“The displaced” correctly means displaced people in B.
C and D use their articles appropriately.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): A trireme was a highly manoeuvrable ancient warship powered by the three rows of oars, designed by Mediterranean civilisations.

question.en: Read the sentences provided in options A, B, C, and D carefully. While three of the sentences are grammatically sound, one contains an “article usage” error. Identify the option with the error. [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The telescope detected so distant a galaxy that its cosmic light took over thirteen billion years to reach the observatory's deep-space sensors.

2.en: The gallery curator remarked that it was quite masterpiece, possessing such a luminous quality that onlookers were instantly captivated.

3.en: What an extraordinary performance the understudy delivered tonight, stepping into the lead role with such absolute composure!

4.en: What fascinating behavioural adaptations deep-sea organisms display when surviving under extreme hydrostatic pressure!

solution.en:
Rule: “Quite” precedes the indefinite article in “quite a + singular noun.”
Option B should read “it was quite a masterpiece.”
“So distant a galaxy” is correct in A, and “What an extraordinary performance” is correct in C.
D correctly uses the plural noun without an article.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): The gallery curator remarked that it was quite masterpiece, possessing such a luminous quality that onlookers were instantly captivated.

question.en:
Identify the word in this sentence that contains an error.
This information is irrelevant with our current topic. [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Irrelevant” is followed by “to,” not “with.”
Correct sentence: “This information is irrelevant to our current topic.”
The erroneous word is “with.”
The remaining words are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): with.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The management had the interns (1)/ to submit their reports (2)/ before the review committee (3)/ arrived for evaluation. (4) [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Causative “have + object” is followed by the bare infinitive.
Part (2) should read “submit their reports,” not “to submit.”
The structure is “had the interns submit.”
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
She is a honest leader with integrity. [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Use “an” before a vowel sound.
“Honest” begins with a silent “h,” so its first sound is a vowel.
Correct sentence: “She is an honest leader with integrity.”
The erroneous article is “a.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): a.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The economic indicators, though initially showing signs of recovery, (1)/ were eventually deemed insufficiently compelling (2)/ to warrant an upward revision of interest rates (3)/ by most analysts who had doubted its trajectory. (4) [SSC CGL 14/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The plural antecedent “indicators” requires “their,” not “its.”
Part (4) should read “who had doubted their trajectory.”
The pronoun must agree with the plural economic indicators.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): (4).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
He came across with an old friend at the conference. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Come across someone” means meet someone unexpectedly; no “with” is used.
Correct sentence: “He came across an old friend at the conference.”
The erroneous phrase is “across with.”
“Come across with” can mean provide something, which is not the intended meaning.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): conference.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a lexical error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: The sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) As the affix body governing international aviation safety, the organisation possesses / (Q) the unilateral authority to ground entire commercial fleets if a systemic manufacturing defect / (R) is uncovered within critical propulsion or avionics architectures, forcing / (S) global aerospace manufacturers into immediate, mandatory retrofitting cycles. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Apex body” means the highest governing organization.
Segment P incorrectly uses “affix,” which means attach.
Correct wording: “As the apex body governing international aviation safety …”
The remaining segments are lexically sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): P.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a lexical error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: The sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) According to the criminal profiling matrix, behavioural analysts noted that / (Q) the serial arsonist's distinct bogus operandi involved using highly refined chemical accelerants / (R) inside abandoned industrial warehouses, establishing a predictable tactical signature / (S) that ultimately allowed law enforcement to map and predict future geographic targets. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Modus operandi” means a characteristic method of operation.
Segment Q incorrectly uses “bogus operandi.”
Correct wording: “the serial arsonist's distinct modus operandi …”
The remaining segments are lexically sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): Q.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a grammatical, syntactic, or idiomatic error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: Every sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) The multi-billion dollar corporate acquisition fell through / (Q) during the final phase of executive negotiations / (R) because the target subsidiary stubbornly refused to comply to / (S) the parent company’s stringent data security architecture guidelines. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The standard construction is “comply with.”
Segment R incorrectly uses “comply to.”
Correct wording: “refused to comply with the parent company’s guidelines.”
The other segments are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): R.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a grammatical, syntactic, or idiomatic error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: Every sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) Instructed to flesh out them before submitting the documentation to the regulatory board, / (Q) the chief immunologist meticulously expanded the safety validation parameters / (R) of the experimental mRNA vaccine candidate, effectively mitigating any potential grounds / (S) for a structural patent rejection or clinical trial delay. [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: An object pronoun comes between the verb and particle: “flesh them out.”
Segment P incorrectly places “them” after the full phrasal verb.
Correct wording: “Instructed to flesh them out …”
The remaining segments are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): P.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Despite of the warnings (1)/ he ventured into the forest (2)/ without any gear (3)/ or backup plan. (4) [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Despite” is not followed by “of.”
Part (1) should read “Despite the warnings” or “In spite of the warnings.”
The preposition “of” is redundant.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The diplomat tried to brush off (1)/ the allegations but the press (2)/ kept pressing on (3)/ until he broke out. (4) [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Break down” means lose emotional control; “break out” means escape or begin suddenly.
Part (4) should read “until he broke down.”
The context requires an emotional collapse under pressure.
The other phrasal verbs are appropriate.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): (4).

question.en:
Spot the error in the following sentence and identify the INCORRECT part.
I have been waiting since two hours for the bus. [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Use “for” with a duration and “since” with a starting point.
“Two hours” is a duration, so use “for two hours.”
“Since” would require a point such as “since 8 a.m.”
The erroneous phrase is “since two hours.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): since two hours.

question.en:
Spot the error in the following sentence and identify the INCORRECT part.
She is good with mathematics but weak in physics. [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The idiomatic adjective–preposition pair is “good at mathematics.”
“Good with” generally refers to handling people or things.
“Weak in physics” is acceptable.
The erroneous phrase is “good with mathematics.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): good with mathematics.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
If he was knowing the answer (1)/ he would have responded (2)/ confidently in the interview (3)/ yesterday. (4) [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Know” is a stative verb and is not normally used in continuous form.
Part (1) should read “If he had known the answer” for an unreal past condition.
“Was knowing” is unidiomatic.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Her avowed neutrality (1)/ in the interdepartmental conflict (2)/ was belied by (3)/ her covert support to one faction. (4) [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The standard preposition after “support” is “for.”
Part (4) should read “her covert support for one faction.”
“Support to” is not the intended construction here.
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): (4).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
She plays the piano (1)/ very good (2)/ considering she started (3)/ just a year ago. (4) [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb “plays” requires the adverb “well,” not the adjective “good.”
Part (2) should read “very well.”
“Good” can modify a noun but not the action of playing.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
Not only the students (1)/ but also the faculty members (2)/ was concerned about (3)/ the accreditation results. (4) [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: With “not only … but also,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
The nearer subject “faculty members” is plural.
Part (3) should read “were concerned about.”
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): (3).

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The professor was appreciative (1)/ with the student's effort (2)/ in curating the bibliography (3)/ in multiple citation styles. (4) [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Appreciative of” is the standard construction.
Part (2) should read “of the student’s effort.”
“Appreciative with” is unidiomatic.
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en: Choose the grammatically INCORRECT sentence. [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The workers have been demanding their wages for over a month

2.en: The newly built highway connects Delhi to Agra seamlessly

3.en: She did not realise that she was supposed to submit the form by yesterday

4.en: The committee have decided to postpone the event

solution.en:
Rule: “Committee” is treated as singular in the intended usage.
Correct sentence: “The committee has decided to postpone the event.”
The other sentences use acceptable verb forms and structures.
“By yesterday” is awkward but denotes the expected deadline.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): The committee have decided to postpone the event.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The committee discussed about the proposal (1)/ for over two hours (2)/ but failed to reach (3)/ any conclusion. (4) [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Discuss” is transitive and is not followed by “about.”
Part (1) should read “The committee discussed the proposal.”
“Talked about the proposal” would also be correct.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Spot the error in the following sentence and identify the INCORRECT part.
She is good in English and Mathematics. [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The idiomatic construction is “good at” a subject or skill.
Correct sentence: “She is good at English and Mathematics.”
“Good in” is not appropriate for academic proficiency.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): good in.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The employee were (1)/ pulled out (2)/ of the task (3)/ for failing to keep it up. (4) [SSC CGL 23/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The singular subject “employee” takes “was.”
Part (1) should read “The employee was.”
“Were” requires a plural subject.
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Spot the error in the following sentence and identify the INCORRECT part.
Each of the players were awarded a certificate of appreciation. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: “Each of + plural noun” takes a singular verb.
The head word is “each,” so use “was awarded.”
Correct sentence: “Each of the players was awarded a certificate.”
The erroneous phrase is “were awarded.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): were awarded.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The manager had left (1)/ before the team arrives (2)/ causing confusion (3)/ about the agenda. (4) [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The past perfect “had left” requires a later simple-past reference.
Part (2) should read “before the team arrived.”
“Arrives” incorrectly shifts into the present.
The remaining parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): (2).

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
We arrived at a Himalayas before sunrise. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Mountain ranges take the definite article “the.”
Correct sentence: “We arrived at the Himalayas before sunrise.”
The indefinite article “a” is incorrect.
The other words are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): a.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a lexical error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: The sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) Despite a lucid awareness of catastrophic epidemiological outcomes, / (Q) active smokers frequently suffer from severe confident dissonance, / (R) systematically deploying deeply flawed psychological defence mechanisms to manipulate their internal narrative, / (S) minimise perceived vulnerability, and ultimately preserve the habituated patterns of their addictive behaviour. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The established term is “cognitive dissonance.”
Segment Q incorrectly uses “confident dissonance.”
It means psychological discomfort from holding conflicting beliefs or actions.
The other segments are lexically sound.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): Q.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a lexical error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: The sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) The prime minister faced intense scrutiny from legislative oversight committees / (Q) after appointing his brother-in-law to head the central bank, a nepotistic appointment / (R) widely criticised as a blatant conflict of impress by anti-corruption watchdogs / (S) demanding an immediate, independent inquiry into executive overreach. [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Conflict of interest” is the standard expression.
Segment R incorrectly uses “conflict of impress.”
The appointment allegedly created competing personal and public interests.
The other segments are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): R.

question.en:
Identify the error in the sentence.
I bought the pair of shoes from the online store. [SSC CGL 27/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Use “a pair of shoes” for a nonspecific purchase.
Correct sentence: “I bought a pair of shoes from the online store.”
“The” would require a pair already identified in context.
The erroneous word is “the.”

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): the.

question.en:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
She is married with a banker (1)/ and has been living in London (2)/ for the past five years (3)/ with her family. (4) [SSC CGL 27/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: “Married to someone” is the standard construction.
Part (1) should read “She is married to a banker.”
“Married with” is unidiomatic.
The other parts are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): (1).

question.en:
Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
If Pushpa Latha have (A)/ passed the law course, (B)/ she would have (C)/ become a lawyer. (D) [SSC CGL 27/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Third conditional uses “if + subject + had + past participle.”
Segment A should read “If Pushpa Latha had.”
The result “would have become” confirms the unreal past.
The other segments are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): If Pushpa Latha have (A).

question.en:
Identify the word in this sentence that contains an error.
She was married with a diplomat from Spain. [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: “Married to someone” is the standard construction.
Correct sentence: “She was married to a diplomat from Spain.”
The erroneous word is “with.”
The other words are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): with.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a grammatical, syntactic, or idiomatic error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: Every sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) Intending to phase out them by the conclusion of the hardware lifecycle, / (Q) the Chief Technology Officer systematically replaced the legacy mainframe servers / (R) with a decentralised, quantum-resistant cloud computing network / (S) to optimise real-time data processing across all global subsidiaries. [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: An object pronoun comes between the verb and particle: “phase them out.”
Segment P incorrectly uses “phase out them.”
Correct wording: “Intending to phase them out …”
The remaining segments are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): P.

question.en:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a grammatical, syntactic, or idiomatic error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: Every sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)
(P) Backed by comprehensive chemical analysis from independent environmental scientists, / (Q) the manufacturing consortium was finally forced to face up the reality / (R) of its severe heavy-metal contamination of the local watershed / (S) and initiate an immediate multi-million dollar soil reclamation project. [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The phrasal verb is “face up to” a reality.
Segment Q omits the preposition “to.”
Correct wording: “forced to face up to the reality.”
The other segments are correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): Q.

question.en:
Read the sentence below carefully. Choose the option (A/B/C) that best improves the sentence. If the sentence is already correct, select Option D (No improvement required).
