question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions:

The menstrual cycle, frequently distilled into reductive explanations within mainstream discourse, constitutes a complex, finely-tuned hormonal symphony that underpins female reproductive viability. Typically spanning around 28 days—though significant interindividual variability persists—the cycle is anatomically and biochemically demarcated into four sequential phases: menstruation, the follicular phase, ovulation, and the luteal phase.

Menstruation initiates with the systematic desquamation of the functional layer of the endometrium, an event precipitated by the precipitous decline in circulating levels of estrogen and progesterone following an unfertilized ovulatory event. Thereafter, during the follicular phase, anterior pituitary secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) catalyses the recruitment and maturation of ovarian follicles. A single dominant follicle subsequently prevails, secreting escalating quantities of estrogen to promote proliferative thickening of the endometrial lining in anticipation of potential zygote implantation.

Mid-cycle, ovulation ensues, triggered by an acute surge of luteinizing hormone (LH), culminating in the release of an oocyte into the fallopian tube — a transient but critical window of maximal fertility. In the absence of fertilization, the luteal phase commences: the residual follicular structure, now termed the corpus luteum, secretes progesterone to stabilize the endometrial architecture. Without embryonic implantation, corpus luteum regression ensues, hormonal concentrations diminish sharply, and the cyclical endometrial shedding recommences.

Despite the endogenous predictability of this sequence, the menstrual cycle exhibits considerable vulnerability to extrinsic perturbations — including psychosocial stressors, systemic illnesses, and environmental variables — underscoring the intricate interplay between endocrine function and broader homeostatic mechanisms.


Identify the correct transformation of the sentence.
“Menstruation initiates with the systematic desquamation of the functional layer of the endometrium.” Which option correctly transforms it into a passive voice without changing the meaning? [SSC CGL 07/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The functional layer of the endometrium is systematically desquamated, initiating menstruation.

2.en: Menstruation is initiating by the desquamation of the functional layer.

3.en: The systematic endometrium desquamates itself to initiate menstruation.

4.en: The menstruation systematically desquamates the functional layer of the endometrium.

solution.en:
Rule: In passive voice, the object becomes the subject and the simple present takes “is/are + past participle”.
“The functional layer” becomes the subject, and “initiates with the systematic desquamation” is expressed as “is systematically desquamated.”
Option 2 uses the incorrect form “is initiating”; option 3 changes the agent and meaning; option 4 remains active and adds an unnecessary article.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): The functional layer of the endometrium is systematically desquamated, initiating menstruation.

According to the passage, what is the primary function of the corpus luteum during the luteal phase? [SSC CGL 07/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To trigger menstruation by lowering progesterone.

2.en: To secrete hormones that maintain endometrial integrity.

3.en: To stimulate another round of follicle maturation.

solution.en:
Corpus luteum: progesterone secretion and endometrial support.
“The residual follicular structure, now termed the corpus luteum, secretes progesterone to stabilize the endometrial architecture.”
Thus, it maintains the endometrial lining during the luteal phase.
Lowering progesterone leads to shedding, not its primary function; follicle maturation belongs to the follicular phase; dissolution follows only when implantation does not occur.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): To secrete hormones that maintain endometrial integrity.

Choose the correct form of the verb for the blank:
“Despite the endogenous predictability of this sequence, the menstrual cycle ___ considerable vulnerability to extrinsic perturbations.” [SSC CGL 07/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: A singular subject takes a singular present-tense verb.
The subject “the menstrual cycle” is singular, so “exhibits” is correct.
Completed sentence: “The menstrual cycle exhibits considerable vulnerability to extrinsic perturbations.”
“Exhibit” is plural, “exhibiting” cannot serve as the finite verb here, and “exhibited” changes the general present fact to the past.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): exhibits.

solution.en:
Desquamation (सतही परत का झड़ना) = shedding of a surface layer of cells.
“Menstruation initiates with the systematic desquamation of the functional layer of the endometrium.”
The menstrual context makes “shedding of the surface layer” the precise meaning.
Thickening is proliferation; hormone secretion is a glandular action; cell multiplication is proliferation, not shedding.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): Shedding of the surface layer.

What is the closest synonym for the word “precipitous” as used in the passage? [SSC CGL 07/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Precipitous (अचानक, तीव्र) = sudden and very steep or rapid.
Abrupt (अचानक) = happening suddenly ✔
Gradual (क्रमिक) = occurring slowly by degrees
Moderate (मध्यम) = average in intensity or amount
Predictable (पूर्वानुमानित) = able to be foreseen
More synonyms: sudden, sharp, rapid.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): Abrupt.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

High above the city, on a tall column, stood the statue of the Happy Prince. The statue was covered with thin leaves of fine gold. It had two bright sapphires for eyes, and a large red ruby shone on the hilt of its sword.

The people of the city greatly admired the statue. “It is as beautiful as a weathercock,” remarked a Town Councillor who wished to be known for his artistic taste. “However, it is not quite as useful,” he added, fearing that others might consider him impractical.

A sensible mother pointed towards the statue and said to her little boy, who was crying for the moon, “Why can’t you behave like the Happy Prince? The Happy Prince never cries for anything.”

“I am glad that someone in the world is completely happy,” muttered a disappointed man as he looked at the magnificent statue.

The Charity Children, dressed in bright scarlet cloaks and clean white pinafores, saw the statue while leaving the cathedral. “The Happy Prince looks just like an angel,” they said.

“How do you know what an angel looks like?” asked the Mathematical Master. “You have never seen one.”

“We have seen angels in our dreams,” replied the children. The Mathematical Master frowned because he did not approve of children dreaming.

One night, a little Swallow flew over the city. His friends had already left for Egypt, but he had stayed behind because he was in love with a beautiful Reed. He had met the Reed in the spring while chasing a yellow moth along the river and stopped to speak to her.


Why did the Town Councillor add that the statue was “not quite as useful” as a weathercock? [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: He feared that people might regard him as an impractical person.

2.en: He believed that public statues should always serve a practical purpose.

3.en: He considered the statue less attractive than an ordinary weathercock.

4.en: He wanted the statue to be removed from the tall column.

solution.en:
Reason: He wanted to protect his reputation for practicality.
“He added, fearing that others might consider him impractical.”
This directly explains his qualification.
He does not demand usefulness from every statue, call it less attractive, or seek its removal.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): He feared that people might regard him as an impractical person.

4.en: He disapproved of children accepting dreams as a source of knowledge.

solution.en:
Reason: He rejected dreaming as a valid activity or source of knowledge.

The children had cited angels seen in dreams, which explains his response.
Disrespect, cathedral-only description and deliberate invention are not suggested.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): He disapproved of children accepting dreams as a source of knowledge.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

High above the city, on a tall column, stood the statue of the Happy Prince. The statue was covered with thin leaves of fine gold. It had two bright sapphires for eyes, and a large red ruby shone on the hilt of its sword.

The people of the city greatly admired the statue. “It is as beautiful as a weathercock,” remarked a Town Councillor who wished to be known for his artistic taste. “However, it is not quite as useful,” he added, fearing that others might consider him impractical.

A sensible mother pointed towards the statue and said to her little boy, who was crying for the moon, “Why can’t you behave like the Happy Prince? The Happy Prince never cries for anything.”

“I am glad that someone in the world is completely happy,” muttered a disappointed man as he looked at the magnificent statue.

The Charity Children, dressed in bright scarlet cloaks and clean white pinafores, saw the statue while leaving the cathedral. “The Happy Prince looks just like an angel,” they said.

“How do you know what an angel looks like?” asked the Mathematical Master. “You have never seen one.”

“We have seen angels in our dreams,” replied the children. The Mathematical Master frowned because he did not approve of children dreaming.

One night, a little Swallow flew over the city. His friends had already left for Egypt, but he had stayed behind because he was in love with a beautiful Reed. He had met the Reed in the spring while chasing a yellow moth along the river and stopped to speak to her.


Which of the following best describes the irony in the mother’s statement to her child? [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She expects a young child to understand the artistic value of a golden statue.

2.en: She holds up an unfeeling, inanimate object as a model of perfect emotional behaviour.

3.en: She praises the Prince’s behaviour while ignoring his immense material wealth.

4.en: She scolds her child for crying while she herself is acting impatiently.

solution.en:
Irony: A lifeless statue is presented as a model for controlling human emotion.
“Why can’t you behave like the Happy Prince? The Happy Prince never cries for anything.”
The statue cannot feel or cry, making the comparison emotionally unreasonable.
Artistic appreciation, material wealth and the mother’s impatience are not the central irony.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): She holds up an unfeeling, inanimate object as a model of perfect emotional behaviour.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions:

The evolution of computers is typically divided into generations, each characterized by significant technological breakthroughs. The First Generation (1940-1956) operated on vacuum tubes, devices that were large, inefficient, and prone to overheating. Programming was tedious, requiring direct interaction with machine language, limiting user accessibility.

With the Second Generation (1956-1963) came transistors, replacing vacuum tubes and greatly enhancing reliability while reducing size and cost. High-level programming languages like COBOL and FORTRAN appeared, making computers more versatile.

The Third Generation (1964-1971) introduced integrated circuits, allowing thousands of electronic components to fit onto a single chip. Computers became smaller, faster, and more powerful. Operating systems began to emerge, enabling machines to run multiple applications simultaneously.

The Fourth Generation (1971-present) saw the invention of the microprocessor, condensing the central processing unit onto a single chip. This innovation ushered in the era of personal computers, making technology widely accessible to businesses and households alike.

Now, in the Fifth Generation, research focuses on artificial intelligence, machine learning, and quantum computing. These developments aim not only to enhance computational speed and storage but also to enable machines to mimic human reasoning and decision-making processes. As technology evolves, the boundary between human capabilities and machine intelligence continues to blur, promising both unprecedented opportunities and profound ethical challenges.


Identify the correct tense used in the sentence:
“With the Second Generation (1956-1963) came transistors, replacing vacuum tubes and greatly enhancing reliability.” [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Tense: Simple Past
“Came” is the simple past form of “come” and describes a completed historical development.
The participles “replacing” and “enhancing” add accompanying results but do not change the main tense.
No “have/has” or “had + past participle” construction appears.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): Simple Past.

What is the meaning of the word “ushered in” as used in the passage? [SSC CGL 08/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Ushered in (आरंभ किया) = introduced or marked the beginning of something.
Ignored (अनदेखा किया) = paid no attention to
Delayed (विलंबित किया) = made late
Introduced (प्रस्तुत/आरंभ किया) = brought into use for the first time ✔
Removed (हटाया) = took away
More synonyms: initiated, launched, inaugurated.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): Introduced.

question.en:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

In a narrow street inhabited by struggling artists, two young artists, Sue and Johnsy, lived together in a modest apartment. During a severe winter, Johnsy contracted pneumonia and gradually lost both her strength and her desire to recover. From her bed, she could see an old ivy vine clinging to the wall of a neighbouring building. As the cold wind tore away its leaves, she developed the strange belief that her life would end when the final leaf fell.

Sue tried to dismiss this belief as irrational, but Johnsy continued to watch the vine with increasing despair. An elderly painter named Behrman lived downstairs. Although he had spoken for years about producing a masterpiece, he had never created anything that fulfilled his ambition. When Sue told him about Johnsy’s condition, he appeared angry at her superstition but was deeply concerned.

That night, a violent storm swept through the city. By morning, Johnsy expected the vine to be completely bare. Yet one leaf remained firmly attached to the wall. It survived another day of wind and rain. Its apparent endurance stirred something within her. She began to feel ashamed that a fragile leaf could resist the storm while she had surrendered hope.

Johnsy slowly recovered. Sue later revealed that the leaf was not real. Behrman had painted it on the wall during the storm and had died of pneumonia soon afterwards. His masterpiece was never displayed in a gallery, but it restored a human being’s will to live.


What does Johnsy’s belief about the falling ivy leaves reveal about her mental condition? [SSC CGL 10/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She had become indifferent to Sue’s concern.

2.en: She had linked her survival to an irrational belief.

3.en: She had misunderstood the cause of her illness.

4.en: She had lost confidence in medical treatment.

solution.en:
Johnsy’s despair takes the form of a morbid superstition.
“She developed the strange belief that her life would end when the final leaf fell.”
She irrationally connects her survival to the vine.
Indifference to Sue, misunderstanding pneumonia and distrust of treatment are not stated.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): She had linked her survival to an irrational belief.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions:

The Big Bang Theory, far from being a mere speculative construct, stands as the most widely endorsed cosmological model explaining the origin and evolution of the universe. Approximately 13.8 billion years ago, the universe emerged from an unimaginably dense and hot singularity — a state where conventional physics collapses under extreme conditions. Within fractions of a second, an exponential inflationary expansion occurred, smoothing out initial irregularities and setting the stage for cosmic structure formation.

As the universe expanded, it cooled, permitting the formation of subatomic particles and, eventually, simple atomic nuclei during the epoch of nucleosynthesis. Several hundred thousand years later, the universe cooled enough for electrons and nuclei to combine into neutral atoms, an event known as recombination, thereby rendering the universe transparent to radiation. The residual glow from this era, observable today as the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) radiation, offers profound empirical support for the Big Bang model.

However, the theory does not escape philosophical and scientific quandaries. It leaves unanswered the very genesis of the singularity itself and cannot yet reconcile quantum mechanics with general relativity at cosmic scales. Furthermore, anomalies within the CMB, the existence of dark matter and dark energy, and the precise rate of cosmic expansion (Hubble tension) continue to perplex scientists.

In essence, while the Big Bang Theory illuminates the universe's evolution post-singularity with remarkable coherence, it simultaneously unveils deep epistemological and empirical mysteries, suggesting that humanity's understanding of cosmic origins remains tantalizingly incomplete.


In the sentence “The Big Bang Theory, far from being a mere speculative construct, stands as the most widely endorsed cosmological model...”,
Identify the grammatical role of the phrase “far from being a mere speculative construct.” [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 2]

3.en: Noun phrase acting as the subject

solution.en:
Function: Adverbial phrase modifying “stands.”
“Far from being a mere speculative construct” is a contrastive phrase: it tells us in what manner the theory stands (not as a mere guess, but as the most endorsed model).
Phrases beginning with “far from + -ing” work adverbially and attach to the main verb, here “stands”.
It does not describe the noun “Theory” like an adjective, it is not the subject, and it does not modify “construct”, which lies inside the phrase itself.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): Adverbial phrase modifying “stands”.

Patterns (प्रतिमान) = regular arrangements
Deviations (विचलन) = departures from a norm ✔
Explanations (स्पष्टीकरण) = reasons or accounts

Read the passage and answer the questions:

The Big Bang Theory, far from being a mere speculative construct, stands as the most widely endorsed cosmological model explaining the origin and evolution of the universe. Approximately 13.8 billion years ago, the universe emerged from an unimaginably dense and hot singularity — a state where conventional physics collapses under extreme conditions. Within fractions of a second, an exponential inflationary expansion occurred, smoothing out initial irregularities and setting the stage for cosmic structure formation.

As the universe expanded, it cooled, permitting the formation of subatomic particles and, eventually, simple atomic nuclei during the epoch of nucleosynthesis. Several hundred thousand years later, the universe cooled enough for electrons and nuclei to combine into neutral atoms, an event known as recombination, thereby rendering the universe transparent to radiation. The residual glow from this era, observable today as the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) radiation, offers profound empirical support for the Big Bang model.

However, the theory does not escape philosophical and scientific quandaries. It leaves unanswered the very genesis of the singularity itself and cannot yet reconcile quantum mechanics with general relativity at cosmic scales. Furthermore, anomalies within the CMB, the existence of dark matter and dark energy, and the precise rate of cosmic expansion (Hubble tension) continue to perplex scientists.

In essence, while the Big Bang Theory illuminates the universe's evolution post-singularity with remarkable coherence, it simultaneously unveils deep epistemological and empirical mysteries, suggesting that humanity's understanding of cosmic origins remains tantalizingly incomplete.


Which of the following best encapsulates the central limitation of the Big Bang Theory according to the passage? [SSC CGL 12/10/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Its inability to explain chemical evolution

2.en: Its dependence solely on mathematical modeling

3.en: Its failure to explain the singularity and reconcile major physical theories

4.en: Its disregard for observational evidence like the CMB

solution.en:
Limitation: The origin of the singularity and the conflict between physical theories remain unresolved.
“It leaves unanswered the very genesis of the singularity itself and cannot yet reconcile quantum mechanics with general relativity.”
Chemical evolution and mathematical dependence are not identified as the central limitation.
The CMB supports rather than is disregarded by the theory.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): Its failure to explain the singularity and reconcile major physical theories.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

As Dorothy and her companions approached the Emerald City, admiration was tempered by uneasiness. From afar, its towers gleamed like precious stones, creating an impression of extraordinary wealth. At the gate, however, every visitor was compelled to wear green spectacles. The Guardian claimed that the glasses protected the eyes from the city’s dazzling brilliance, but the travellers suspected a subtler purpose: the lenses might manipulate perception and make the city appear more magnificent than it actually was.

Within the walls, green dominated every aspect of life. Buildings seemed to be made of green marble, emeralds glittered on the walls, citizens wore green garments, and even the goods in the shops conformed to the same carefully maintained colour scheme. The uniformity suggested not merely decoration, but deliberate control over appearances.

Yet the splendour failed to quiet the travellers’ anxiety. Dorothy wished to return home, the Scarecrow sought intelligence, the Tin Woodman desired a heart, and the Lion longed for courage. Their private deficiencies mattered more than the city’s outward grandeur. Their hopes rested on the mysterious Wizard, although no citizen could clearly describe him. When informed that they would meet him separately, they felt increasingly vulnerable, for they had expected to draw courage from one another's presence.


What did the compulsory use of green spectacles lead the travellers to suspect? [SSC CGL 13/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The city was genuinely too bright for ordinary vision.

2.en: Visitors were required to follow local customs unquestioningly.

3.en: The Guardian intended to manipulate visitors’ perception of the city.

4.en: The Guardian wanted to distinguish citizens from outsiders.

solution.en:
Suspicion: The spectacles served perceptual manipulation rather than protection.
“The lenses might manipulate perception and make the city appear more magnificent than it actually was.”
This directly states their concern.
Genuine brightness, unquestioning custom and distinguishing outsiders are not their suspicion.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): The Guardian intended to manipulate visitors’ perception of the city.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions:

The menstrual cycle, frequently distilled into reductive explanations within mainstream discourse, constitutes a complex, finely-tuned hormonal symphony that underpins female reproductive viability. Typically spanning around 28 days—though significant interindividual variability persists—the cycle is anatomically and biochemically demarcated into four sequential phases: menstruation, the follicular phase, ovulation, and the luteal phase.

Menstruation initiates with the systematic desquamation of the functional layer of the endometrium, an event precipitated by the precipitous decline in circulating levels of estrogen and progesterone following an unfertilized ovulatory event. Thereafter, during the follicular phase, anterior pituitary secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) catalyses the recruitment and maturation of ovarian follicles. A single dominant follicle subsequently prevails, secreting escalating quantities of estrogen to promote proliferative thickening of the endometrial lining in anticipation of potential zygote implantation.

Mid-cycle, ovulation ensues, triggered by an acute surge of luteinizing hormone (LH), culminating in the release of an oocyte into the fallopian tube—a transient but critical window of maximal fertility. In the absence of fertilization, the luteal phase commences: the residual follicular structure, now termed the corpus luteum, secretes progesterone to stabilize the endometrial architecture. Without embryonic implantation, corpus luteum regression ensues, hormonal concentrations diminish sharply, and the cyclical endometrial shedding recommences.

Despite the endogenous predictability of this sequence, the menstrual cycle exhibits considerable vulnerability to extrinsic perturbations—including psychosocial stressors, systemic illnesses, and environmental variables—underscoring the intricate interplay between endocrine function and broader homeostatic mechanisms.


Identify the correct transformation of the sentence.
“Menstruation initiates with the systematic desquamation of the functional layer of the endometrium.”
Which option correctly transforms it into a passive voice without changing the meaning? [SSC CGL 15/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The functional layer of the endometrium is systematically desquamated, initiating menstruation.

2.en: Menstruation is initiating by the desquamation of the functional layer.

3.en: The systematic endometrium desquamates itself to initiate menstruation.

4.en: The menstruation systematically desquamates the functional layer of the endometrium.

solution.en:
Rule: The object of “desquamates” becomes the passive subject.
“The functional layer … is systematically desquamated” preserves the process that initiates menstruation.
B uses an incorrect passive verb form; C changes the agent and structure.
D remains active and reverses the intended relationship.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): The functional layer of the endometrium is systematically desquamated, initiating menstruation.

Read the passage and answer the questions:

The pyramids, most famously epitomized by the colossal structures at Giza, remain one of humanity's most astonishing architectural feats. Constructed over 4,500 years ago, these geometric marvels continue to baffle engineers, historians, and archaeologists alike. Despite centuries of scrutiny, the exact methodologies employed in their construction elude definitive explanation.

The prevailing theories suggest that a combination of ingenuity, rudimentary tools, and sheer human determination enabled the transportation and placement of multi-ton limestone blocks with astonishing precision. However, emerging hypotheses propose that the ancient Egyptians may have leveraged techniques far more sophisticated than previously acknowledged, including the potential use of water to reduce friction on desert sands or the employment of lost materials like early forms of concrete.

Beyond the mechanics of their assembly, the pyramids encapsulate profound cultural and religious significance. They were not merely tombs, but cosmic monuments designed to ensure the pharaohs’ transcendence into the afterlife, aligning meticulously with celestial bodies to reflect a deeper metaphysical order. The internal labyrinths, adorned with cryptic hieroglyphs and symbolic chambers, further attest to a civilization whose understanding of mathematics, astronomy, and theology was remarkably advanced.

Today, while modern technology such as satellite imaging and muon radiography peels back some layers of mystery, the pyramids still guard many of their secrets. They stand not merely as relics of a bygone era, but as enduring testaments to humanity's timeless pursuit of greatness, ingenuity, and the eternal enigma of existence itself.


Identify the correct form of the verb that should fill the blank:
“The pyramids, most famously epitomized by the colossal structures at Giza, ___ one of humanity's most astonishing architectural feats.” [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The plural subject “the pyramids” takes the plural verb “are.”
The intervening descriptive phrase does not change subject–verb agreement.
The sentence states a present general fact.
“Is” and “was” are singular; “were” incorrectly shifts to past.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): are.

They stand not merely as relics of a bygone era, but as enduring testaments to humanity's timeless pursuit of greatness, ingenuity, and the eternal enigma of existence itself.


According to the passage, which of the following best describes the primary cultural significance of the pyramids? [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 1]

3.en: They represented a metaphysical journey linked to celestial alignment.

4.en: They were primarily built to showcase wealth to rival civilizations.

solution.en:
Text evidence: The pyramids ensured transcendence into the afterlife and aligned with celestial bodies.
They reflected a metaphysical order rather than merely serving as tombs.
Military power, general spiritual power and displays of wealth are not the passage’s primary emphasis.
The metaphysical journey and celestial alignment are explicitly linked.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): They represented a metaphysical journey linked to celestial alignment.

Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

In an era of saturation with new media, the dissemination of counterfeit information in the media has become an irreversible threat to social cohesion. Though disinformation in the past was at least contained by geography and language, fabricated fiction in the present sweeps around the world in a matter of seconds—presenting themselves as respectful journalism, falsified photos, or taken-out-of-context morsels of fact. The pervasiveness of social media has made fact-checking more of a reactive than a proactive role and generally permits distortions to become established before correction can occur.

The effects extend far beyond simple confusion. Manipulated media drive political action, fuel communal tensions, and erode trust in democratic institutions. If citizens cannot tell good sources of information from bad, democratic processes suffer, as public opinion is shaped by vetted facts rather than viral disinformation. In worst-case scenarios, disinformation has even prompted violence or destroyed health initiatives, as witnessed around the global pandemic.

Added to this problem is also the emergence of algorithm-fed aggregation of content, which further enriches echo chambers. The user is constantly given information that will most likely reinforce their current beliefs, creating a loop of feedback that legitimates falsity and bars dissonant truths. In the meantime, deepfakes and AI-generated content introduced an aspect of novelty in the crisis wherein fabrication is basically rendered indistinguishable from truth.

To combat this threat, however, calls for more than simply technical counter-response; it calls for media literacy, institutional disclosure, and a recasting of how truth is built and presented in a post-truth world. Without profound systemic change, the distinction between information and manipulation will always be blurry, threatening the very foundations of informed citizenship.


According to the passage, what has made fake media a uniquely modern threat? [SSC CGL 16/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Text evidence: Fabricated fiction now sweeps around the world in seconds.
Earlier disinformation was contained by geography and language.
Instant global digital diffusion therefore defines the uniquely modern threat.
The other options are not identified in the passage.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): Instant global digital diffusion.

Climate change is beginning to impact Indian agriculture in visible ways. Rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall, and extreme weather events are affecting crop yields across states like Punjab, Maharashtra, and West Bengal. Traditional farming calendars are becoming unreliable, forcing farmers to adapt by switching to shorter-duration or drought-resistant crops. Government initiatives like PM Fasal Bima Yojana provide crop insurance, but awareness and timely claim settlements remain a concern. Experts suggest combining modern weather forecasting with traditional knowledge to help farmers make informed decisions. Without timely interventions, food security and farmer livelihoods may face long-term risks.


How is climate change affecting Indian farmers? [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Text evidence: Rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall and extreme weather affect crop yields.
Farmers face declining production and unreliable agricultural calendars.
Profits, work hours and predictability are not identified as benefits.
The passage instead warns of risks to livelihoods.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): Reducing crop yields.

Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

Over the past few years, Indian destination weddings have grown into a thriving economic trend, pushing the traditional boundaries between festivals and enterprises. Exclusive domain of royal dynasties and Bollywood royalty earlier, today, such grand affairs are aspiring to be undertaken by a new generation of prosperous businesspeople and NRIs. Udaipur, Jaipur, and Kovalam have become top locations, providing a carefully designed synthesis of history, hospitality, and spectacle.

The ripple effect of such weddings on the economy is profound. A single lavish wedding can create a supply chain from hotels to caterers to artisans to transportation providers and even bouquet sellers in the neighbourhood. Industry estimates place the Indian wedding industry's contribution at close to 3.7 lakh crore each year, with destination weddings making up a large portion of it.

But there are conditions. Local infrastructure gets strained during peak season, especially in small towns that have not been designed for high-density tourism. Furthermore, environmental issues—such as over-exploitation of resources, waste, and energy use—are not addressed adequately. State governments are keen on the economic boost, but regulatory frameworks do not keep pace, being set more to facilitate business than ensure sustainability.

Essentially, Indian destination weddings walk the tightrope between cultural spectacle and business venture. The economic impetus that they generate in the short term is certain, but concerns regarding their ecological impact as well as their inclusivity persist to command policy scrutiny.


What does the passage primarily emphasize about destination weddings in India? [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Text evidence: Destination weddings walk the tightrope between cultural spectacle and business venture.
They combine historical and cultural display with major economic activity.
The passage does not say they are losing popularity or are eco-friendly.
Urban burden is only one concern, not the central emphasis.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4): They combine culture and commerce.

The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA) is a social security scheme guaranteeing 100 days of paid work annually to rural households. It is a lifeline during agricultural off-seasons and in times of economic stress. MNREGA work typically includes land development, irrigation, and road repair. The program is demand-driven, meaning jobs are provided when people request them. In states like Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh, MNREGA has helped reduce migration to cities. Critics, however, raise concerns over delayed wage payments and corruption in fund disbursal. To enhance transparency, digital attendance systems and direct bank transfers have been introduced.


What does MNREGA guarantee? [SSC CGL 22/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Text evidence: MNREGA guarantees 100 days of paid work annually to rural households.
It provides employment during agricultural off-seasons and economic stress.
It is not a ration, education or farm-loan programme.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): 100 days of paid rural work.

This workforce comprises freelancers, delivery personnel, ride-share drivers, and others working on a task-by-task basis. Read the passage and answer the questions:

Dinosaurs, the magnificent archosaurs that dominated terrestrial ecosystems for over 160 million years, continue to captivate both scientific inquiry and popular imagination. Emerging during the Triassic Period approximately 230 million years ago, dinosaurs diversified rapidly, exploiting ecological niches ranging from apex predation to herbivorous grazing.

Paleontological evidence reveals that dinosaurs were not monolithic; they represented an extraordinary array of morphologies, behaviours, and metabolic strategies. Contrary to the once-prevailing image of sluggish, cold-blooded reptiles, current research suggests that many species, particularly theropods, exhibited endothermic traits and dynamic activity levels. Feathers, once considered exclusive to modern birds, have been identified in numerous non-avian dinosaur fossils, suggesting evolutionary continuity rather than abrupt transformation.

The Cretaceous-Palaeogene (K-Pg.) extinction event, approximately 66 million years ago, precipitated the demise of non-avian dinosaurs, plausibly triggered by an asteroid impact combined with extensive volcanic activity. This cataclysmic shift not only eradicated dominant dinosaurian lineages but also catalysed mammalian diversification, reshaping evolutionary trajectories.

Yet, despite monumental advances in technology—from CT-scanning fossilized bones to analysing isotopic signatures—critical enigmas persist. Questions concerning precise dinosaurian physiology, social behaviour, and even the nuances of their extinction dynamics remain partially speculative. Moreover, the fossil record itself is inherently incomplete, biased toward preservation-friendly environments, thereby skewing interpretations.

Ultimately, the study of dinosaurs transcends mere historical reconstruction; it probes the intricate processes of evolution, adaptation, and extinction—processes that remain profoundly relevant in an era of accelerating environmental change.


In the sentence “Dinosaurs, the magnificent archosaurs that dominated terrestrial ecosystems, continue to captivate both scientific inquiry and popular imagination,” what is the grammatical function of the clause “that dominated terrestrial ecosystems”? [SSC CGL 24/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: A relative clause modifies a noun and begins with a relative pronoun.
“That dominated terrestrial ecosystems” modifies “archosaurs.”
“That” refers to the archosaurs and acts as the clause’s subject.
It is not a noun, adverbial or prepositional clause.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): Relative Clause.

As artificial intelligence (AI) continues to redefine industries and professions, the indispensability of uniquely human skills has become increasingly pronounced. In an era where algorithms can perform routine tasks with unerring precision and speed, individuals must cultivate abilities that machines cannot easily replicate—namely critical thinking, creativity, emotional intelligence, and adaptability.

The 21st-century workforce demands more than technical literacy; it necessitates a dynamic synergy between hard skills and soft skills. Technical prowess alone, once sufficient, now risks obsolescence unless it is paired with problem-solving capacities and an innovative mind set. Employers increasingly value candidates who can not only interpret data but also infer nuanced insights, which can not only program software but also envision novel applications beyond conventional frameworks.

Moreover, resilience and the ability to unlearn and relearn swiftly are no longer optional traits but survival mechanisms. As AI accelerates change, static knowledge bases decay at an unprecedented pace. Workers who cling rigidly to out-dated competencies inevitably find themselves outpaced, while those who embrace lifelong learning carve niches even amidst automation's relentless advance.

Ultimately, it is not a competition between humans and machines, but between adaptive and static mind sets. In this fluid landscape, mastering uniquely human attributes is not merely advantageous; it is existentially imperative.


Identify the sentence with the correct use of the semicolon: [SSC CGL 27/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The 21st-century workforce demands more than technical literacy, it necessitates a dynamic synergy between hard and soft skills.

2.en: The 21st-century workforce demands more than technical literacy; it necessitates a dynamic synergy between hard and soft skills.

3.en: The 21st-century workforce demands more than technical literacy: it necessitates a dynamic synergy between hard and soft skills.

4.en: The 21st-century workforce demands more than technical literacy; necessitating a dynamic synergy between hard and soft skills.

solution.en:
Rule: A semicolon can join two closely related independent clauses.
Both “the workforce demands …” and “it necessitates …” are complete clauses.
Option B joins them correctly without a conjunction.
A is a comma splice; D leaves a fragment after the semicolon.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): The 21st-century workforce demands more than technical literacy; it necessitates a dynamic synergy between hard and soft skills.

In today's corporate environment, dysfunctional behavior—taken in the form of manipulation, exclusion, harassment, or passive aggression—is a pervasive undertone. Typically hidden behind professional demeanour or performance targets, such behavior erodes organizational trust and destroys psychological safety. It does not necessarily start from open hostility; instead, it is often system-based—rooted in workplace hierarchies, incentive schemes, and tacit cultural norms.

Evidence demonstrates that organizations plagued by toxic dynamics experience higher attrition rates, lower employee participation, and higher mental illness. In contrast to conventional management presumptions, productivity is not enhanced by pressure or fear; instead, productivity quietly declines as workers disengage, do a poor job, or abandon work altogether. Toxic cultures also stifle innovation, as fear of retaliation deters dissension and exploration—both essential in competitive markets.

Leaders tend to misread short-term deliverables as long-term effectiveness, failing to notice that constant exposure to toxicity undermines an organization's strength and overall efficacy. Exacerbating the situation is the tendency to heroize “difficult geniuses”—individual workers who excel on their own but undermine team morale. This glamorization creates a vicious cycle where toxicity is overlooked if it is combined with profitability.

Abating such conduct is beyond the reach of compliance training or loose ethical guidelines. It necessitates structural change, open accountability, and a culture shift that emphasizes shared well-being as well as monetary profit. Without these, the corporate poison will still disguise itself as greatness, leaving a trail of burnout, turnover, and reduced institutional integrity. “generate 10 hard mcq on this passage with solution and description”.

Manipulation, exclusion and passive aggression operate as concealed patterns.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3): Through hidden patterns and performance pressure.

Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

In the 21st century, outer space has evolved from a scientific frontier into a geopolitical theatre where diplomacy, commerce, and national security intersect. The concept of space diplomacy—using cooperation and negotiation in outer space affairs as tools of statecraft—has become central to the foreign policy strategies of both emerging and established powers. It is no longer sufficient for nations to launch satellites; they must now navigate orbital politics. The strategic importance of space assets—from communication satellites to Earth observation systems—has redefined the contours of sovereignty and surveillance. Increasingly, countries are leveraging space-based capabilities for soft power projection, offering satellite data to developing nations, sharing launch infrastructure, and even co-developing space missions. Such cooperation enhances diplomatic goodwill while simultaneously extending geopolitical influence. India’s space diplomacy, for instance, has matured from technological self-reliance to regional leadership. The South Asia Satellite, launched by ISRO in 2017, was a watershed moment—offering communication and meteorological services to neighbouring countries as a “gift.” However, even as such projects are framed as acts of regional solidarity, they reinforce India's leadership narrative in the subcontinent. Yet, this domain is not without contest. The increasing militarization of space, signaled by the creation of dedicated space forces and the testing of anti-satellite weapons (ASATs), adds a layer of strategic mistrust. The absence of updated, binding international treaties governing weaponization and satellite security further complicates multilateral coordination. At the same time, the entry of private players into the space ecosystem introduces commercial diplomacy. Tech giants and start-ups now collaborate with governments in dual-use ventures—civilian technologies with potential military applications. As regulatory frameworks struggle to keep pace, diplomacy must adapt not only to intergovernmental negotiations but also to corporate interests. In essence, space diplomacy is about managing cooperation amid competition. As Low Earth Orbit becomes increasingly crowded and lunar exploration re-emerges as a theatre of contest, future diplomacy must balance ambition with restraint. Nations that excel in this balance will shape not just the future of outer space—but also the geopolitical alignments back on Earth.


According to the passage, why is space no longer a purely scientific domain? [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 1]

2.en: It involves geopolitical, strategic, and economic stakes

3.en: Nations have stopped funding basic research

4.en: Only private companies now operate in space

solution.en:
Text evidence: Space now joins diplomacy, commerce and national security.
Orbital assets affect sovereignty, surveillance and geopolitical influence.
The passage does not claim full commercialization or an end to research.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): It involves geopolitical, strategic, and economic stakes.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions:

The Big Bang Theory, far from being a mere speculative construct, stands as the most widely endorsed cosmological model explaining the origin and evolution of the universe. Approximately 13.8 billion years ago, the universe emerged from an unimaginably dense and hot singularity—a state where conventional physics collapses under extreme conditions. Within fractions of a second, an exponential inflationary expansion occurred, smoothing out initial irregularities and setting the stage for cosmic structure formation.

As the universe expanded, it cooled, permitting the formation of subatomic particles and, eventually, simple atomic nuclei during the epoch of nucleosynthesis. Several hundred thousand years later, the universe cooled enough for electrons and nuclei to combine into neutral atoms, an event known as recombination, thereby rendering the universe transparent to radiation. The residual glow from this era, observable today as the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) radiation, offers profound empirical support for the Big Bang model.

However, the theory does not escape philosophical and scientific quandaries. It leaves unanswered the very genesis of the singularity itself and cannot yet reconcile quantum mechanics with general relativity at cosmic scales. Furthermore, anomalies within the CMB, the existence of dark matter and dark energy, and the precise rate of cosmic expansion (Hubble tension) continue to perplex scientists.

In essence, while the Big Bang Theory illuminates the universe's evolution post-singularity with remarkable coherence, it simultaneously unveils deep epistemological and empirical mysteries, suggesting that humanity's understanding of cosmic origins remains tantalizingly incomplete.


In the sentence “The Big Bang Theory, far from being a mere speculative construct, stands as the most widely endorsed cosmological model...”, identify the grammatical role of the phrase “far from being a mere speculative construct.” [SSC CGL 28/10/26 Shift 2]

3.en: Noun phrase acting as the subject

solution.en:
Rule: “Far from + gerund” is an adverbial phrase of contrast that qualifies the verb.
“Far from being a mere speculative construct” tells us in what manner the theory stands – not as speculation, but as the most endorsed model.
It is set off by commas and contrasts with the predicate “stands as the most widely endorsed cosmological model”.
It is not the subject, and “construct” is a noun inside the phrase, so options 3 and 4 are wrong.

Hence, the correct answer is option (1): Adverbial phrase modifying “stands”.

The CMB contains unexplained irregularities that perplex scientists.
“Deviations” is the closest synonym.
Patterns, explanations and confirmations do not express irregularity.

Hence, the correct answer is option (2): Deviations.

question.en: How many points are awarded for a successful "touchdown" in American Football? [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 2]
question.hi: अमेरिकी फ़ुटबॉल में सफल "टचडाउन" के लिए कितने अंक दिए जाते हैं? [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (3) – 6
A touchdown, scored by carrying or catching the ball in the opponent's end zone, is worth 6 points.


Important Points:
• After a touchdown, a kick (extra point) gives 1 point and a two-point conversion gives 2 points.
• A field goal = 3 points; a safety = 2 points.
• The NFL championship game is called the Super Bowl.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (3) – 6
विरोधी के एंड ज़ोन (End zone) में गेंद ले जाकर या पकड़कर किया गया टचडाउन (Touchdown) 6 अंक का होता है।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• टचडाउन के बाद किक (अतिरिक्त अंक) से 1 अंक और टू-पॉइंट कन्वर्ज़न से 2 अंक मिलते हैं।
• फ़ील्ड गोल (Field goal) = 3 अंक; सेफ्टी (Safety) = 2 अंक।
• NFL के चैंपियनशिप मैच को सुपर बाउल (Super Bowl) कहते हैं।

question.en: Which Indian cricket stadium hosted the 2023 ICC World Cup final? [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 2]
question.hi: किस भारतीय क्रिकेट स्टेडियम ने 2023 ICC विश्व कप फाइनल की मेज़बानी की? [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (3) – Narendra Modi Stadium
The 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup final was played on 19 November 2023 at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, where Australia beat India.


Important Points:
• Narendra Modi Stadium (formerly Motera) is the world's largest cricket stadium (capacity about 1,32,000).
• Australia won its sixth ODI World Cup title; Travis Head was Player of the Match.
• Wankhede (Mumbai) hosted the 2011 World Cup final won by India.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (3) – नरेंद्र मोदी स्टेडियम
2023 ICC पुरुष क्रिकेट विश्व कप फाइनल 19 नवंबर 2023 को नरेंद्र मोदी स्टेडियम, अहमदाबाद में खेला गया, जहाँ ऑस्ट्रेलिया ने भारत को हराया।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• नरेंद्र मोदी स्टेडियम (पूर्व नाम मोटेरा) विश्व का सबसे बड़ा क्रिकेट स्टेडियम है (क्षमता लगभग 1,32,000)।
• ऑस्ट्रेलिया ने अपना छठा वनडे विश्व कप जीता; ट्रैविस हेड प्लेयर ऑफ द मैच रहे।
• वानखेड़े (मुंबई) में 2011 विश्व कप फाइनल हुआ था, जिसे भारत ने जीता।

question.en: Which Indian tennis player, at age 43, set the Open Era record by winning the Australian Open 2024 men’s doubles title? [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi: किस भारतीय टेनिस खिलाड़ी ने 43 वर्ष की आयु में ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन 2024 पुरुष युगल खिताब जीतकर ओपन युग का रिकॉर्ड बनाया? [SSC CGL 30/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (3) – Rohan Bopanna
Rohan Bopanna, partnering Matthew Ebden (Australia), won the 2024 Australian Open men's doubles and became the oldest man in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam title.


Important Points:
• In the same year Bopanna became the oldest World No. 1 in men's doubles.
• Australian Open is played on hard courts in Melbourne; it is the first Grand Slam of the year.
• Bopanna's earlier Grand Slam: 2017 French Open mixed doubles (with Gabriela Dabrowski).
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (3) – रोहन बोपन्ना
रोहन बोपन्ना ने मैथ्यू एबडेन (ऑस्ट्रेलिया) के साथ 2024 ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन पुरुष युगल जीता और ओपन युग में ग्रैंड स्लैम खिताब जीतने वाले सबसे उम्रदराज़ पुरुष बने।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• उसी वर्ष बोपन्ना पुरुष युगल में सबसे उम्रदराज़ विश्व नंबर 1 बने।
• ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन मेलबर्न में हार्ड कोर्ट पर खेला जाता है; यह वर्ष का पहला ग्रैंड स्लैम है।
• बोपन्ना का पूर्व ग्रैंड स्लैम: 2017 फ्रेंच ओपन मिश्रित युगल (गैब्रिएला डाब्रोवस्की के साथ)।

question.en: Which Indian sport involves riding a horse and attempting to spear a small target? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: किस भारतीय खेल में घुड़सवारी करते हुए एक छोटे लक्ष्य को भाले से भेदने का प्रयास किया जाता है? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – Tent Pegging
In Tent Pegging, a rider at full gallop uses a lance or sword to pierce and carry away a small ground target (peg).


Important Points:
• Tent pegging is a cavalry sport, popular in the Indian Army (61st Cavalry).
• Polo originated in Manipur (Sagol Kangjei); Imphal's polo ground is among the oldest.
• Jousting is a medieval European sport; Rodeo is associated with the USA.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – टेंट पेगिंग
टेंट पेगिंग में घुड़सवार तेज़ दौड़ते घोड़े पर भाले या तलवार से ज़मीन पर रखे छोटे लक्ष्य (खूँटी) को भेदकर उठा ले जाता है।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• टेंट पेगिंग घुड़सवार सेना का खेल है, जो भारतीय सेना (61वीं कैवेलरी) में लोकप्रिय है।
• पोलो की उत्पत्ति मणिपुर (सगोल कंगजेई) में हुई।
• जूस्टिंग मध्यकालीन यूरोपीय खेल है; रोडियो अमेरिका से जुड़ा है।

question.en: In which year was Kho-Kho included in the South Asian Games? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: खो-खो को दक्षिण एशियाई खेलों में किस वर्ष शामिल किया गया? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – 2016
Kho-Kho was included for the first time in the 12th South Asian Games held at Guwahati and Shillong in 2016, and India won gold in both men's and women's events.


Important Points:
• The first Kho-Kho World Cup was held in New Delhi in January 2025; India won both men's and women's titles.
• Kho-Kho is played with 12 players per side, of whom 9 take the field.
• Governing body in India: Kho-Kho Federation of India (1955).
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – 2016
खो-खो को 2016 में गुवाहाटी और शिलांग में आयोजित 12वें दक्षिण एशियाई खेलों में शामिल किया गया, जहाँ भारत ने पुरुष और महिला दोनों वर्गों में स्वर्ण जीता: 2016।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• पहला खो-खो विश्व कप जनवरी 2025 में नई दिल्ली में हुआ; भारत ने पुरुष और महिला दोनों खिताब जीते।
• खो-खो में प्रत्येक टीम में 12 खिलाड़ी होते हैं, जिनमें से 9 मैदान में उतरते हैं।
• भारत में शासी निकाय: खो-खो फेडरेशन ऑफ इंडिया (1955)।

question.en: Who among the following was the first Indian to win a Grand Slam title? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: निम्नलिखित में से ग्रैंड स्लैम खिताब जीतने वाले पहले भारतीय कौन थे? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (1) – Mahesh Bhupati
Mahesh Bhupathi became the first Indian to win a Grand Slam title when he won the 1997 French Open mixed doubles with Rika Hiraki of Japan.


Important Points:
• Bhupathi completed a career Grand Slam in mixed doubles.
• Leander Paes won Olympic bronze at Atlanta 1996.
• Sania Mirza was the first Indian woman to win a Grand Slam (2009 Australian Open mixed doubles).
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (1) – महेश भूपति
महेश भूपति 1997 फ्रेंच ओपन मिश्रित युगल जापान की रिका हिराकी के साथ जीतकर ग्रैंड स्लैम खिताब जीतने वाले पहले भारतीय बने।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• भूपति ने मिश्रित युगल में करियर ग्रैंड स्लैम पूरा किया।
• लिएंडर पेस ने अटलांटा 1996 ओलंपिक में कांस्य जीता।
• सानिया मिर्ज़ा ग्रैंड स्लैम जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय महिला थीं (2009 ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन मिश्रित युगल)।

question.en: At the Paris Olympics 2024, which Indian female shooter won an Olympic medal in the 10m Air Pistol event, becoming the first-ever woman from India to do so? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: पेरिस ओलंपिक 2024 में किस भारतीय महिला निशानेबाज़ ने 10 मीटर एयर पिस्टल स्पर्धा में ओलंपिक पदक जीतकर ऐसा करने वाली पहली भारतीय महिला बनने का गौरव प्राप्त किया? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – Manu Bhaker
Manu Bhaker won bronze in the women's 10m Air Pistol at Paris 2024, becoming India's first woman shooter to win an Olympic medal.


Important Points:
• She also won bronze in 10m Air Pistol mixed team with Sarabjot Singh – first Indian since Independence to win two medals at one Olympics.
• India won 6 medals at Paris 2024 (1 silver, 5 bronze).
• Manu Bhaker received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna in 2025.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – मनु भाकर
मनु भाकर ने पेरिस 2024 में महिला 10 मीटर एयर पिस्टल में कांस्य जीता और ओलंपिक पदक जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय महिला निशानेबाज़ बनीं।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• उन्होंने सरबजोत सिंह के साथ 10 मीटर एयर पिस्टल मिश्रित टीम में भी कांस्य जीता – स्वतंत्रता के बाद एक ओलंपिक में दो पदक जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय।
• पेरिस 2024 में भारत ने 6 पदक जीते (1 रजत, 5 कांस्य)।
• मनु भाकर को 2025 में मेजर ध्यानचंद खेल रत्न मिला।

question.en: Which Indian athlete is known for her achievements in sprint running and is often referred to as "Dhing Express"? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]
question.hi: कौन-सी भारतीय एथलीट स्प्रिंट दौड़ में अपनी उपलब्धियों के लिए जानी जाती है और जिसे अक्सर "ढिंग एक्सप्रेस" कहा जाता है? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (3) – Hima Das
Hima Das, from Dhing village in Nagaon district, Assam, is called the "Dhing Express". In 2018 she became the first Indian to win a gold at the IAAF World U-20 Championships (400 m).


Important Points:
• P.T. Usha – "Payyoli Express"; current President of the Indian Olympic Association.
• Anju Bobby George – first Indian to win a medal at the World Athletics Championships (long jump bronze, 2003).
• Dutee Chand – national record holder in women's 100 m.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (3) – हिमा दास
असम के नगाँव ज़िले के ढिंग गाँव की हिमा दास को "ढिंग एक्सप्रेस" कहा जाता है। 2018 में वह IAAF विश्व अंडर-20 चैंपियनशिप (400 मीटर) में स्वर्ण जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय बनीं।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• पी.टी. उषा – "पय्योली एक्सप्रेस"; वर्तमान में भारतीय ओलंपिक संघ की अध्यक्ष।
• अंजू बॉबी जॉर्ज – विश्व एथलेटिक्स चैंपियनशिप में पदक जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय (लंबी कूद कांस्य, 2003)।
• दुती चंद – महिला 100 मीटर की राष्ट्रीय रिकॉर्डधारी।

question.en: The Singh Sisters from Punjab contributed to India's rise in which underrepresented court sport? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]
question.hi: पंजाब की सिंह बहनों ने किस कम प्रतिनिधित्व वाले कोर्ट खेल में भारत के उत्थान में योगदान दिया? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (3) – Basketball
The Singh Sisters – Prashanti, Akanksha, Divya, Pratima and Priyanka Singh – represented India in basketball and played a major role in the growth of women's basketball in the country.


Important Points:
• Prashanti Singh received the Arjuna Award (2017) and the Padma Shri (2019).
• Basketball was invented by James Naismith in 1891; 5 players per side.
• Governing body: Basketball Federation of India; international body FIBA.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (3) – बास्केटबॉल
सिंह बहनों – प्रशांति, आकांक्षा, दिव्या, प्रतिमा और प्रियंका सिंह – ने बास्केटबॉल में भारत का प्रतिनिधित्व किया और देश में महिला बास्केटबॉल के विकास में बड़ी भूमिका निभाई।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• प्रशांति सिंह को अर्जुन पुरस्कार (2017) और पद्म श्री (2019) मिला।
• बास्केटबॉल का आविष्कार जेम्स नाइस्मिथ ने 1891 में किया; प्रत्येक टीम में 5 खिलाड़ी।
• शासी निकाय: बास्केटबॉल फेडरेशन ऑफ इंडिया; अंतर्राष्ट्रीय निकाय FIBA।

question.en: Where was the location of the 2017 Senior National Judo Championships? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]
question.hi: 2017 सीनियर राष्ट्रीय जूडो चैंपियनशिप का आयोजन स्थल कहाँ था? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (4) – Chennai
The Senior National Judo Championships 2016-17 were held in Chennai (Tamil Nadu) on 26–27 February 2017, organised under the Judo Federation of India.


Important Points:
• Judo originated in Japan; founded by Jigoro Kano in 1882.
• Judo became an Olympic sport at Tokyo 1964.
• Judo terms: Ippon, Waza-ari, Tatami, Judogi.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (4) – चेन्नई
सीनियर राष्ट्रीय जूडो चैंपियनशिप 2016-17 का आयोजन 26–27 फरवरी 2017 को चेन्नई (तमिलनाडु) में जूडो फेडरेशन ऑफ इंडिया के अधीन किया गया।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• जूडो की उत्पत्ति जापान में हुई; 1882 में जिगोरो कानो ने इसकी स्थापना की।
• जूडो टोक्यो 1964 में ओलंपिक खेल बना।
• जूडो की शब्दावली: इप्पोन, वाज़ा-अरी, तातामी, जूडोगी।

question.en: Which principle makes an athlete responsible for any substance found in their sample? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 3]
question.hi: कौन-सा सिद्धांत खिलाड़ी को उसके नमूने में पाए गए किसी भी पदार्थ के लिए उत्तरदायी बनाता है? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – Strict Liability
Under the World Anti-Doping Code, the principle of strict liability makes each athlete responsible for any prohibited substance found in his or her sample, whether or not it was used intentionally.


Important Points:
• WADA was established in 1999; HQ Montreal, Canada.
• India's NADA functions under the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022.
• WADA publishes the Prohibited List every year.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – कठोर दायित्व
विश्व डोपिंग रोधी संहिता के तहत कठोर दायित्व (Strict liability) का सिद्धांत प्रत्येक खिलाड़ी को उसके नमूने में पाए गए किसी भी प्रतिबंधित पदार्थ के लिए उत्तरदायी बनाता है, चाहे उसका उपयोग जानबूझकर हुआ हो या नहीं।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• WADA की स्थापना 1999 में हुई; मुख्यालय मॉन्ट्रियल, कनाडा।
• भारत का NADA राष्ट्रीय डोपिंग रोधी अधिनियम, 2022 के तहत कार्य करता है।
• WADA हर वर्ष प्रतिबंधित सूची (Prohibited List) जारी करता है।

question.en: Which of the following correctly matches the width measurements of the pommel horse in gymnastics? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 3]
question.hi: जिम्नास्टिक्स में पॉमेल हॉर्स की चौड़ाई के मापों का निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सही मिलान है? [SSC CGL 01/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – Top – 35 cm, Bottom – 30 cm
As per FIG apparatus norms, the body of the pommel horse is 35 cm wide at the top and 30 cm at the bottom.


Important Points:
• Length of the pommel horse is about 160 cm and height about 115 cm; pommels are 12 cm high.
• Pommel horse is a men's artistic gymnastics event.
• Gymnastics is governed by FIG (Fédération Internationale de Gymnastique), HQ Lausanne.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – ऊपर – 35 cm, नीचे – 30 cm
FIG उपकरण मानकों के अनुसार पॉमेल हॉर्स का शरीर ऊपर 35 cm और नीचे 30 cm चौड़ा होता है।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• पॉमेल हॉर्स की लंबाई लगभग 160 cm और ऊँचाई लगभग 115 cm होती है; पॉमेल 12 cm ऊँचे होते हैं।
• पॉमेल हॉर्स पुरुषों की कलात्मक जिम्नास्टिक्स स्पर्धा है।
• जिम्नास्टिक्स का शासी निकाय FIG है, मुख्यालय लुसाने।

question.en: What is the term for a score of zero in tennis? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: टेनिस में शून्य अंक को क्या कहा जाता है? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (1) – Love
In tennis, a score of zero is called "Love". Points in a game are counted as Love (0), 15, 30, 40 and game.


Important Points:
• Deuce – score of 40–40; Advantage – the point won just after deuce.
• Ace – a serve that the opponent fails to touch.
• Four Grand Slams: Australian Open, French Open (clay), Wimbledon (grass), US Open.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (1) – लव
टेनिस में शून्य अंक को "लव (Love)" कहा जाता है। एक गेम में अंक लव (0), 15, 30, 40 और गेम के रूप में गिने जाते हैं।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• ड्यूस – 40–40 का स्कोर; एडवांटेज – ड्यूस के ठीक बाद जीता गया अंक।
• ऐस – ऐसी सर्विस जिसे प्रतिद्वंद्वी छू भी न सके।
• चार ग्रैंड स्लैम: ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन, फ्रेंच ओपन (क्ले), विंबलडन (घास), यूएस ओपन।

question.en: The final of the 2017 FIFA U-17 World Cup was held in Kolkata. Which stadium hosted the final match? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: 2017 फीफा अंडर-17 विश्व कप का फाइनल कोलकाता में हुआ था। किस स्टेडियम ने फाइनल मैच की मेज़बानी की? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (1) – Salt Lake Stadium
The final of the 2017 FIFA U-17 World Cup was played at the Salt Lake Stadium (Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan), Kolkata, on 28 October 2017; England beat Spain 5–2.


Important Points:
• It was the first FIFA tournament hosted by India.
• Salt Lake Stadium is one of India's largest football stadiums.
• Golden Ball: Phil Foden; Golden Boot: Rhian Brewster (both England).
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (1) – साल्ट लेक स्टेडियम
2017 फीफा अंडर-17 विश्व कप का फाइनल 28 अक्टूबर 2017 को कोलकाता के साल्ट लेक स्टेडियम (विवेकानंद युवा भारती क्रीड़ांगन) में खेला गया; इंग्लैंड ने स्पेन को 5–2 से हराया।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• यह भारत द्वारा आयोजित पहला फीफा टूर्नामेंट था।
• साल्ट लेक स्टेडियम भारत के सबसे बड़े फुटबॉल स्टेडियमों में से एक है।
• गोल्डन बॉल: फिल फोडेन; गोल्डन बूट: रियान ब्रूस्टर (दोनों इंग्लैंड)।

question.en: What is “En Passant” in chess? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: शतरंज में “एन पासां (En Passant)” क्या है? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (1) – Special pawn capture
En passant ("in passing") is a special pawn capture: if a pawn moves two squares and lands beside an enemy pawn, that enemy pawn may capture it as if it had moved only one square, but only on the very next move.


Important Points:
• Other special moves: castling and pawn promotion.
• Chess originated in India as Chaturanga (Gupta period).
• Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster (1988); D. Gukesh became the youngest World Champion in 2024.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (1) – प्यादे की विशेष कैप्चर चाल
एन पासां ("गुज़रते हुए") प्यादे की विशेष कैप्चर चाल है: यदि कोई प्यादा दो खाने चलकर विरोधी प्यादे के बगल में आ जाए, तो विरोधी प्यादा उसे ऐसे पकड़ सकता है मानो वह केवल एक खाना चला हो, परंतु केवल अगली चाल में ही।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• अन्य विशेष चालें: कैसलिंग (Castling) और प्यादा प्रोन्नयन (Pawn promotion)।
• शतरंज की उत्पत्ति भारत में चतुरंग के रूप में हुई (गुप्त काल)।
• विश्वनाथन आनंद भारत के पहले ग्रैंडमास्टर (1988) थे; डी. गुकेश 2024 में सबसे कम उम्र के विश्व चैंपियन बने।

question.en: Which is correct about the long jump runway and take-off board? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: लंबी कूद के रनवे और टेक-ऑफ बोर्ड के बारे में कौन-सा कथन सही है? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Plasticine indicator width: 1.22 m; placed 3 m from pit
1.hi: प्लास्टिसिन संकेतक की चौड़ाई: 1.22 m; पिट से 3 m दूर

2.en: Take-off board width: 1.22 m; runway length: 20 cm
2.hi: टेक-ऑफ बोर्ड की चौड़ाई: 1.22 m; रनवे की लंबाई: 20 cm

3.en: Runway width: 10 cm; take-off board thickness: 45°
3.hi: रनवे की चौड़ाई: 10 cm; टेक-ऑफ बोर्ड की मोटाई: 45°

4.en: Runway length: 40–45 m; take-off board length: 1.22 m
4.hi: रनवे की लंबाई: 40–45 m; टेक-ऑफ बोर्ड की लंबाई: 1.22 m

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (4) – Runway length: 40–45 m; take-off board length: 1.22 m
As per World Athletics rules, the long jump runway is at least 40 m long (40–45 m) and the take-off board is about 1.22 m long (1.21–1.22 m), 20 cm wide and 10 cm deep.


Important Points:
• Runway width: 1.22 m ± 0.01 m.
• Distance from take-off board to the far end of the landing pit: at least 10 m; board placed 1–3 m from the near end of the pit.
• Long jump world record (men): 8.95 m by Mike Powell (1991).
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (4) – रनवे की लंबाई: 40–45 m; टेक-ऑफ बोर्ड की लंबाई: 1.22 m
विश्व एथलेटिक्स नियमों के अनुसार लंबी कूद का रनवे कम से कम 40 m लंबा (40–45 m) होता है और टेक-ऑफ बोर्ड लगभग 1.22 m लंबा (1.21–1.22 m), 20 cm चौड़ा और 10 cm गहरा होता है।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• रनवे की चौड़ाई: 1.22 m ± 0.01 m।
• टेक-ऑफ बोर्ड से लैंडिंग पिट के दूरस्थ छोर तक दूरी: कम से कम 10 m; बोर्ड पिट के निकट छोर से 1–3 m पर।
• लंबी कूद का विश्व रिकॉर्ड (पुरुष): माइक पॉवेल द्वारा 8.95 m (1991)।

question.en: With 18 Grand Slam titles, who among the following is considered India's most successful tennis players? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 2]
question.hi: 18 ग्रैंड स्लैम खिताबों के साथ, निम्नलिखित में से किसे भारत का सबसे सफल टेनिस खिलाड़ी माना जाता है? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (4) – Leander Paes
Leander Paes has won 18 Grand Slam titles – 8 men's doubles and 10 mixed doubles – making him India's most successful tennis player.


Important Points:
• Paes won the bronze medal at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics (singles).
• He completed a career Grand Slam in both men's doubles and mixed doubles.
• He played in a record 7 Olympic Games (1992–2016); inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2024.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (4) – लिएंडर पेस
लिएंडर पेस ने 18 ग्रैंड स्लैम खिताब – 8 पुरुष युगल और 10 मिश्रित युगल – जीते हैं, जिससे वे भारत के सबसे सफल टेनिस खिलाड़ी हैं।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• पेस ने 1996 अटलांटा ओलंपिक (एकल) में कांस्य पदक जीता।
• उन्होंने पुरुष युगल और मिश्रित युगल दोनों में करियर ग्रैंड स्लैम पूरा किया।
• उन्होंने रिकॉर्ड 7 ओलंपिक खेलों (1992–2016) में भाग लिया; 2024 में अंतर्राष्ट्रीय टेनिस हॉल ऑफ फेम में शामिल।

question.en: Which of the following is not included in the women’s heptathlon? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 2]
question.hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी स्पर्धा महिलाओं के हेप्टाथलॉन में शामिल नहीं है? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (3) – 400 metres
The women's heptathlon has seven events: 100 m hurdles, high jump, shot put, 200 m (day 1) and long jump, javelin throw, 800 m (day 2). 400 m is not part of it.


Important Points:
• The 400 m is part of the men's decathlon (10 events).
• Swapna Barman won India's first heptathlon gold at the 2018 Asian Games.
• Heptathlon world record holder: Jackie Joyner-Kersee (7,291 points).
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (3) – 400 मीटर
महिलाओं के हेप्टाथलॉन में सात स्पर्धाएँ हैं: 100 मीटर बाधा दौड़, ऊँची कूद, गोला फेंक, 200 मीटर (पहला दिन) तथा लंबी कूद, भाला फेंक, 800 मीटर (दूसरा दिन)। 400 मीटर इसमें शामिल नहीं है।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• 400 मीटर पुरुषों के डेकाथलॉन (10 स्पर्धाएँ) का भाग है।
• स्वप्ना बर्मन ने 2018 एशियाई खेलों में भारत का पहला हेप्टाथलॉन स्वर्ण जीता।
• हेप्टाथलॉन विश्व रिकॉर्डधारी: जैकी जॉयनर-केर्सी (7,291 अंक)।

question.en:
Consider the following statements about the Beach Games 2024 held in Diu:
1) Madhya Pradesh topped the medal tally with 18 medals, including 7 golds.
2) Maharashtra won the gold medal in Beach Soccer by defeating Lakshadweep in the final.
Which of the statements is/are correct? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 2]
question.hi:
दीव में आयोजित बीच गेम्स 2024 के बारे में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1) मध्य प्रदेश 7 स्वर्ण सहित 18 पदकों के साथ पदक तालिका में शीर्ष पर रहा।
2) महाराष्ट्र ने फाइनल में लक्षद्वीप को हराकर बीच सॉकर में स्वर्ण पदक जीता।
कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 2]

4.hi: न तो 1 और न ही 2 सही है

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (1) – Only 1 is Correct
At the first-ever Beach Games (Diu, January 2024), landlocked Madhya Pradesh emerged overall champion with 18 medals including 7 golds, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 about the beach soccer final is not correct. Hence Only 1.


Important Points:
• The games were held from 4 to 11 January 2024 at Ghoghla Beach, Diu, under Khelo India.
• Sports included beach soccer, beach volleyball, beach kabaddi, sepak takraw, pencak silat, mallakhamb, sea swimming and tug of war.
• Diu is part of the UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (1) – केवल 1 सही है
पहले बीच गेम्स (दीव, जनवरी 2024) में स्थलरुद्ध मध्य प्रदेश 7 स्वर्ण सहित 18 पदकों के साथ समग्र चैंपियन बना, अतः कथन 1 सही है। बीच सॉकर फाइनल के बारे में कथन 2 सही नहीं है। अतः केवल 1।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• ये खेल खेलो इंडिया के तहत 4 से 11 जनवरी 2024 तक घोघला बीच, दीव में हुए।
• खेलों में बीच सॉकर, बीच वॉलीबॉल, बीच कबड्डी, सेपक टकरा, पेनकक सिलाट, मल्लखंभ, समुद्री तैराकी और रस्साकशी शामिल थे।
• दीव केंद्रशासित प्रदेश दादरा और नगर हवेली तथा दमन और दीव का भाग है।

question.en: Which Indian city hosted the 2010 Commonwealth Games? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 3]
question.hi: किस भारतीय शहर ने 2010 राष्ट्रमंडल खेलों की मेज़बानी की? [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – New Delhi
The XIX Commonwealth Games were held in New Delhi from 3 to 14 October 2010; India finished second with 101 medals (38 gold).


Important Points:
• The main venue was the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, Delhi; mascot "Shera".
• It was the first time India hosted the Commonwealth Games.
• The 2026 Commonwealth Games are being held in Glasgow, Scotland; India will host the 2030 Games in Ahmedabad.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – नई दिल्ली
19वें राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 3 से 14 अक्टूबर 2010 तक नई दिल्ली में हुए; भारत 101 पदकों (38 स्वर्ण) के साथ दूसरे स्थान पर रहा।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• मुख्य स्थल जवाहरलाल नेहरू स्टेडियम, दिल्ली; शुभंकर "शेरा"।
• भारत ने पहली बार राष्ट्रमंडल खेलों की मेज़बानी की।
• 2026 राष्ट्रमंडल खेल ग्लासगो, स्कॉटलैंड में; भारत 2030 खेलों की मेज़बानी अहमदाबाद में करेगा।

question.en: National Team Chess Championship 2024-25 held in ________. [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 3]
question.hi: राष्ट्रीय टीम शतरंज चैंपियनशिप 2024-25 ________ में आयोजित हुई। [SSC CGL 05/10/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (4) – Ahmedabad
The National Team Chess Championship 2024-25 (men and women) was held in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, from 5 to 11 March 2025, organised under the All India Chess Federation.


Important Points:
• Chess governing body in India: All India Chess Federation (AICF), HQ Chennai.
• India won both open and women's gold at the 45th Chess Olympiad, Budapest (2024).
• D. Gukesh became the youngest World Chess Champion in December 2024.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (4) – अहमदाबाद
राष्ट्रीय टीम शतरंज चैंपियनशिप 2024-25 (पुरुष और महिला) अखिल भारतीय शतरंज महासंघ के अधीन 5 से 11 मार्च 2025 तक अहमदाबाद, गुजरात में आयोजित हुई।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• भारत में शतरंज का शासी निकाय: अखिल भारतीय शतरंज महासंघ (AICF), मुख्यालय चेन्नई।
• भारत ने 45वें शतरंज ओलंपियाड, बुडापेस्ट (2024) में ओपन और महिला दोनों स्वर्ण जीते।
• डी. गुकेश दिसंबर 2024 में सबसे कम उम्र के विश्व शतरंज चैंपियन बने।

question.en: How many active players are there per team in a regulation water polo match? [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: नियमित वॉटर पोलो मैच में प्रत्येक टीम में कितने सक्रिय खिलाड़ी होते हैं? [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (3) – 7
In water polo, each team has 7 players in the water – 6 field players and 1 goalkeeper.


Important Points:
• A match has four quarters of 8 minutes of actual play.
• Water polo is governed by World Aquatics (formerly FINA).
• It was one of the first team sports in the modern Olympics (1900).
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (3) – 7
वॉटर पोलो में प्रत्येक टीम के 7 खिलाड़ी पानी में होते हैं – 6 फ़ील्ड खिलाड़ी और 1 गोलकीपर।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• एक मैच में वास्तविक खेल के 8 मिनट के चार क्वार्टर होते हैं।
• वॉटर पोलो का शासी निकाय वर्ल्ड एक्वेटिक्स (पूर्व में FINA) है।
• यह आधुनिक ओलंपिक के पहले टीम खेलों में से एक था (1900)।

question.en: In which year did the National Games of India take place in Jharkhand? [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: भारत के राष्ट्रीय खेल झारखंड में किस वर्ष आयोजित हुए? [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – 2011
The 34th National Games were held in Jharkhand (Ranchi, Jamshedpur and Dhanbad) in February 2011, so the answer is 2011.


Important Points:
• Services (SSCB) topped the medal tally at the 2011 Games.
• 38th National Games were held in Uttarakhand (2025); the 37th in Goa (2023).
• The National Games are conducted by the Indian Olympic Association.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – 2011
34वें राष्ट्रीय खेल फरवरी 2011 में झारखंड (राँची, जमशेदपुर और धनबाद) में आयोजित हुए, अतः उत्तर 2011 है।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• 2011 के खेलों में सर्विसेज़ (SSCB) पदक तालिका में शीर्ष पर रहा।
• 38वें राष्ट्रीय खेल उत्तराखंड (2025) में और 37वें गोवा (2023) में हुए।
• राष्ट्रीय खेलों का आयोजन भारतीय ओलंपिक संघ करता है।

question.en:
Consider the following statements about the grip and placement of the shot in the gliding technique in Shot Put:
1) The shot is held primarily in the palm with fingers loosely wrapped around it.
2) The shot is placed near the jaw bone, just below the ear and over the collar bone.
3) Fingers are spread apart slightly with the thumb providing support while holding the shot.
Which of the statements given above are correct? [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]
question.hi:
गोला फेंक की ग्लाइडिंग तकनीक में गोले की पकड़ और स्थिति के बारे में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1) गोला मुख्य रूप से हथेली में पकड़ा जाता है और उंगलियाँ उसके चारों ओर ढीली लिपटी होती हैं।
2) गोला जबड़े की हड्डी के पास, कान के ठीक नीचे और हंसली (कॉलर बोन) के ऊपर रखा जाता है।
3) गोला पकड़ते समय उंगलियाँ थोड़ी फैली होती हैं और अंगूठा सहारा देता है।
ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं? [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – Only 2 and 3 are Correct
In shot put, the shot rests on the base of the fingers, not in the palm – so statement 1 is wrong. It is placed against the neck below the ear, above the collar bone, with fingers slightly spread and the thumb supporting it. Hence Only 2 and 3.


Important Points:
• The gliding technique is also called the O'Brien technique (Parry O'Brien).
• Shot weight: 7.26 kg (men), 4 kg (women); throwing circle diameter 2.135 m.
• The shot must be put (pushed), not thrown, from the shoulder with one hand.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – केवल 2 और 3 सही हैं
गोला फेंक में गोला उंगलियों के आधार पर टिकता है, हथेली में नहीं – अतः कथन 1 गलत है। इसे कान के नीचे, हंसली के ऊपर गर्दन से सटाकर रखा जाता है, उंगलियाँ थोड़ी फैली होती हैं और अंगूठा सहारा देता है। अतः केवल 2 और 3।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
• ग्लाइडिंग तकनीक को ओ'ब्रायन तकनीक (पैरी ओ'ब्रायन) भी कहते हैं।
• गोले का भार: 7.26 kg (पुरुष), 4 kg (महिला); फेंक वृत्त का व्यास 2.135 m।
• गोले को एक हाथ से कंधे से धकेला (Put) जाता है, फेंका नहीं।

question.en: With which sport is the term "googly" traditionally associated? [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 2]
question.hi: "गुगली" शब्द पारंपरिक रूप से किस खेल से संबंधित है? [SSC CGL 06/10/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct Answer: Option (2) – Cricket
A googly is a deceptive delivery in cricket bowled by a leg-spinner that turns the opposite way (from off to leg for a right-handed batter).


Important Points:
• The googly was invented by England's Bernard Bosanquet; it is also called the "wrong'un".
• Other cricket terms: doosra, yorker, chinaman, bouncer, LBW.
• Hockey terms: penalty corner, bully, dribble; Kabaddi terms: raid, cant, lona.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर: विकल्प (2) – क्रिकेट
गुगली क्रिकेट में लेग-स्पिनर द्वारा फेंकी जाने वाली भ्रामक गेंद है, जो विपरीत दिशा में (दाएँ हाथ के बल्लेबाज़ के लिए ऑफ से लेग की ओर) घूमती है।


महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
